questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current carrying circular loop of radius $2$ cm with unit normal $\hat{n} = \dfrac{\hat{k}+\hat{i}}{\sqrt{2}}$ is placed in a magnetic field, $\vec{B} = B_0(3\hat{i}+2\hat{k})$. If $B_0 = 4\times 10^{-3}$ T and current $I=100\sqrt{2}$ A, the torque experienced by the loop is ________ Wb·A. ($\pi=3.14$)
questions.solution:
The magnetic dipole moment of the current carrying loop is given by $\vec{M} = I A \hat{n}$.

Given radius $r = 2$ cm $= 2 \times 10^{-2}$ m, the area of the loop is:
$A = \pi r^2 = \pi (2 \times 10^{-2})^2 = 4\pi \times 10^{-4}$ m$^2$

Substituting the given values $I = 100\sqrt{2}$ A and $\hat{n} = \dfrac{\hat{i}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{2}}$:
$\vec{M} = (100\sqrt{2}) \times (4\pi \times 10^{-4}) \times \left(\dfrac{\hat{i}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
$\vec{M} = 4\pi \times 10^{-2} (\hat{i}+\hat{k})$ A$\cdot$m$^2$

The torque experienced by the loop in the magnetic field is $\vec{\tau} = \vec{M} \times \vec{B}$.
Given $\vec{B} = 4 \times 10^{-3} (3\hat{i}+2\hat{k})$ T, we have:
$\vec{\tau} = [4\pi \times 10^{-2} (\hat{i}+\hat{k})] \times [4 \times 10^{-3} (3\hat{i}+2\hat{k})]$
$\vec{\tau} = 16\pi \times 10^{-5} [(\hat{i}+\hat{k}) \times (3\hat{i}+2\hat{k})]$

Evaluating the cross product:
$(\hat{i}+\hat{k}) \times (3\hat{i}+2\hat{k}) = (\hat{i} \times 3\hat{i}) + (\hat{i} \times 2\hat{k}) + (\hat{k} \times 3\hat{i}) + (\hat{k} \times 2\hat{k})$
$= 0 + 2(-\hat{j}) + 3(\hat{j}) + 0 = \hat{j}$

Therefore, the torque is:
$\vec{\tau} = 16\pi \times 10^{-5} \hat{j}$

Substituting $\pi = 3.14$:
$\vec{\tau} = 16 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-5} \hat{j} = 50.24 \times 10^{-5} \hat{j} = 5024 \times 10^{-7} \hat{j}$ Wb$\cdot$A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $5$ mg particle carrying a charge of $5\pi\times 10^{-6}$ C is moving with velocity of $(3\hat{i}+2\hat{k})\times 10^{-2}$ m/s in a region having magnetic field $\vec{B} = 0.1\hat{k}$ Wb/m$^2$. It moves a distance of $\alpha$ meter along $\hat{k}$ when it completes $5$ revolutions. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Given:
Mass of the particle, $m = 5 \text{ mg} = 5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ kg}$
Charge, $q = 5\pi \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}$
Velocity, $\vec{v} = (3\hat{i} + 2\hat{k}) \times 10^{-2} \text{ m/s}$
Magnetic field, $\vec{B} = 0.1\hat{k} \text{ Wb/m}^2$

The velocity component parallel to the magnetic field is $v_{\parallel} = 2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m/s}$.

The time period of one revolution is given by:
$T = \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$

Substituting the given values:
$T = \dfrac{2\pi \times 5 \times 10^{-6}}{5\pi \times 10^{-6} \times 0.1} = \dfrac{2}{0.1} = 20 \text{ s}$

The time taken to complete $5$ revolutions is:
$t = 5T = 5 \times 20 = 100 \text{ s}$

The distance moved along the $\hat{k}$ direction (pitch for $5$ revolutions) is:
$\alpha = v_{\parallel} \times t$
$\alpha = 2 \times 10^{-2} \times 100 = 2 \text{ m}$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current of $30$ A each flows in opposite directions in two conducting wires, placed parallel to each other at a distance of $8$ cm. The magnetic field at the mid point between the two wires is __________ $\mu$T. $\left(\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7}\text{ N/A}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Let the distance between the wires be $d = 8\text{ cm}$. The distance of the midpoint from each wire is $r = \dfrac{d}{2} = 4\text{ cm} = 0.04\text{ m}$.

The current in each wire is $I = 30\text{ A}$.

Since the currents flow in opposite directions, the magnetic fields produced by both wires at the midpoint point in the same direction and add up.

The total magnetic field at the midpoint is:

$B_{\text{net}} = B_1 + B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi r}$

Substituting the given values:

$B_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 30}{\pi \times 0.04}$

$B_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{120 \times 10^{-7}}{0.04}$

$B_{\text{net}} = 3000 \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}$

$B_{\text{net}} = 300 \times 10^{-6}\text{ T} = 300\ \mu\text{T}$

Answer: $300$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small cube of side $1$ mm is placed at the centre of a circular loop of radius $10$ cm carrying a current of $2$ A. The magnetic energy stored inside the cube is $\alpha \times 10^{-14}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. ($\mu_o = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ Tm/A, $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at the centre of the circular loop is given by $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$

Substituting the given values, $B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2}{2 \times 0.1} = 4\pi \times 10^{-6}$ T

The magnetic energy density is $u = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$

$u = \dfrac{(4\pi \times 10^{-6})^2}{2 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7}} = \dfrac{16\pi^2 \times 10^{-12}}{8\pi \times 10^{-7}} = 2\pi \times 10^{-5}$ J/m$^3$

The volume of the small cube is $V = (1 \text{ mm})^3 = (10^{-3} \text{ m})^3 = 10^{-9}$ m$^3$

The magnetic energy stored inside the cube is $U = u \times V$

$U = 2\pi \times 10^{-5} \times 10^{-9} = 2\pi \times 10^{-14}$ J

Using $\pi = 3.14$, we get $U = 2 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-14} = 6.28 \times 10^{-14}$ J

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-14}$ J, we get $\alpha = 6.28$

Answer: $6.28$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field of $(3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j})$ T has an acceleration $\left(4\hat{i} - \dfrac{x}{2}\hat{j}\right)$ m/s$^2$. The value of $x$ is __________.
questions.solution:
The magnetic force on a moving charged particle is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

Since the acceleration $\vec{a}$ is in the direction of the magnetic force, it must be perpendicular to the magnetic field $\vec{B}$.

Therefore, the dot product of acceleration and magnetic field is zero:

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{B} = 0$

Substituting the given vectors:

$\left(4\hat{i} - \dfrac{x}{2}\hat{j}\right) \cdot (3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) = 0$

$(4)(3) + \left(-\dfrac{x}{2}\right)(2) = 0$

$12 - x = 0$

$x = 12$

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A circular coil of radius $2$ cm and $125$ turns carries a current of $1$ A. The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.4$ T. The axis of the coil makes an angle of $30°$ with the direction of the magnetic field. The torque acting on the coil is $\alpha \times 10^{-4}$ N.m. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
($\pi=3.14$)
questions.solution:
The magnetic moment of the coil is given by $M = NIA$.

The torque acting on the coil is $\tau = MB \sin\theta = NIAB \sin\theta$.

Substituting the given values:

$\tau = 125 \times 1 \times (\pi \times (0.02)^2) \times 0.4 \times \sin 30^\circ$

$\tau = 125 \times 1 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-4} \times 0.4 \times 0.5$

$\tau = 100\pi \times 10^{-4}$

$\tau = 100 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-4} = 314 \times 10^{-4}$ N.m

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-4}$ N.m, we get $\alpha = 314$.

Answer: $314$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An insulated wire is wound so that it forms a flat coil with $N = 200$ turns. The radius of the innermost turn is $r_1 = 3$ cm, and of the outermost turn $r_2 = 6$ cm. If $20$ mA current flows in it then the magnetic moment will be $\alpha \times 10^{-2}$ A.m$^2$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Let the number of turns per unit radial width be $n = \dfrac{N}{r_2 - r_1}$.

Consider an elemental ring of radius $r$ and width $dr$. The number of turns in this element is $dN = n \, dr$.

The magnetic moment of this elemental ring is $dM = I \, dN \, A = I \left( \dfrac{N}{r_2 - r_1} \, dr \right) (\pi r^2)$.

Integrating from $r_1$ to $r_2$ to find the total magnetic moment $M$:

$M = \int_{r_1}^{r_2} \dfrac{I \pi N}{r_2 - r_1} r^2 \, dr = \dfrac{I \pi N}{3(r_2 - r_1)} (r_2^3 - r_1^3)$

Substituting the given values: $I = 20 \times 10^{-3}$ A, $N = 200$, $r_1 = 0.03$ m, and $r_2 = 0.06$ m:

$M = \dfrac{20 \times 10^{-3} \times \pi \times 200}{3(0.06 - 0.03)} \left( (0.06)^3 - (0.03)^3 \right)$

$M = \dfrac{4\pi}{0.09} (216 \times 10^{-6} - 27 \times 10^{-6})$

$M = \dfrac{4\pi}{0.09} \times 189 \times 10^{-6} = 4\pi \times 2100 \times 10^{-6}$

$M = 84\pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 84 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-4} = 263.76 \times 10^{-4} \approx 2.64 \times 10^{-2}$ A.m$^2$

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-2}$ A.m$^2$, we get $\alpha = 2.64$.

Answer: $2.64$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle having charge $10^{-9}$ C moving in $x$-$y$ plane in fields of $0.4\hat{j}$ N/C and $4 \times 10^{-3} \hat{k}$ T experiences a force of $(4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) \times 10^{-10}$ N. The velocity of the particle at that instant is _______ m/s.
questions.solution:
The Lorentz force experienced by a charged particle is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

Given that the particle moves in the $x$-$y$ plane, its velocity can be written as $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j}$.

Substituting the given values into the force equation:

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} [0.4\hat{j} + (v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j}) \times (4 \times 10^{-3} \hat{k})]$

Using the cross product rules $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$ and $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$:

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} [0.4\hat{j} - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x \hat{j} + 4 \times 10^{-3} v_y \hat{i}]$

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} [4 \times 10^{-3} v_y \hat{i} + (0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x) \hat{j}]$

The given force is $\vec{F} = (4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) \times 10^{-10}$ N, which can be rewritten as:

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} (0.4\hat{i} + 0.2\hat{j})$ N

Comparing the coefficients of $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ from both expressions:

For the $\hat{i}$ component:
$4 \times 10^{-3} v_y = 0.4$
$v_y = \dfrac{0.4}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 100$ m/s

For the $\hat{j}$ component:
$0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x = 0.2$
$4 \times 10^{-3} v_x = 0.2$
$v_x = \dfrac{0.2}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 50$ m/s

Therefore, the velocity of the particle is $\vec{v} = 50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j}$ m/s.

Answer: $50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in the following figures. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are $B_1$ and $B_2$ respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}$ is _______.
questions.solution:
For the first figure, the magnetic field at the centre P is the vector sum of the magnetic fields due to two semi-infinite straight wires and one semicircular arc.

The magnetic field due to the top semi-infinite wire at P is $B_{1a} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ directed into the plane.

The magnetic field due to the bottom semi-infinite wire at P is $B_{1b} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ directed into the plane.

The magnetic field due to the semicircular arc at P is $B_{1c} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4r} = \dfrac{\pi \mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ directed into the plane.

The total magnetic field at P is $B_1 = B_{1a} + B_{1b} + B_{1c} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (1 + 1 + \pi) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (2 + \pi)$.

For the second figure, the magnetic field at the centre Q is the vector sum of the magnetic fields due to one horizontal semi-infinite wire, one semicircular arc, and one vertical semi-infinite wire.

The magnetic field due to the horizontal semi-infinite wire at Q is $B_{2a} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ directed into the plane.

The magnetic field due to the semicircular arc at Q is $B_{2c} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4r} = \dfrac{\pi \mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ directed into the plane.

Since the arc is semicircular, it ends at a point directly below Q. The vertical semi-infinite wire starts from this point and extends downwards, meaning its line of action passes through Q. Therefore, the magnetic field due to this vertical wire at Q is $B_{2b} = 0$.

The total magnetic field at Q is $B_2 = B_{2a} + B_{2b} + B_{2c} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (1 + 0 + \pi) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (1 + \pi)$.

The ratio of the magnetic fields is $\dfrac{B_1}{B_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (2 + \pi)}{\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (1 + \pi)} = \dfrac{2 + \pi}{1 + \pi}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2 + \pi}{1 + \pi}$

questions.q: $1\,\mu$C charge moving with velocity $\vec{v} = \left(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right)$ m/s in the region of magnetic field $\vec{B} = \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\right)$ T. The magnitude of force acting on it is $\sqrt{\alpha} \times 10^{-6}$ N. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.solution:
The magnetic force acting on a moving charge is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

Given:
$q = 1 \, \mu\text{C} = 10^{-6} \text{ C}$
$\vec{v} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$
$\vec{B} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$

Calculating the cross product $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$:
$\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -5 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = \hat{i}(10 - 9) - \hat{j}(-5 - 6) + \hat{k}(3 + 4)$
$\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = \hat{i} + 11\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$

The magnitude of $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$ is:
$|\vec{v} \times \vec{B}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 11^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 121 + 49} = \sqrt{171}$

The magnitude of the force is:
$|\vec{F}| = q |\vec{v} \times \vec{B}| = 10^{-6} \times \sqrt{171} = \sqrt{171} \times 10^{-6} \text{ N}$

Comparing this with the given expression $\sqrt{\alpha} \times 10^{-6} \text{ N}$, we get:
$\alpha = 171$

Answer: $171$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A long cylindrical conductor with large cross section carries an electric current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. Magnetic field due to this current is :
A. maximum at either ends of the conductor and minimum at the midpoint
B. maximum at the axis of the conductor
C. minimum at the surface of the conductor
D. minimum at the axis of the conductor
E. same at all points in the cross-section of the conductor
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For a long cylindrical conductor with uniform current distribution, apply Ampere's law to find the magnetic field.
At distance $r$ from the axis (inside the conductor, $r < R$): $B(r) = \frac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}$ (proportional to $r$)
At the axis ($r = 0$): $B = 0$ (minimum)
At the surface ($r = R$): $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R}$ (maximum)
Analyzing the statements:
A. Maximum at ends and minimum at midpoint - FALSE. This describes behavior along the axis, but the magnetic field depends on radial distance, not axial position.
B. Maximum at the axis of the conductor - FALSE. The field is zero at the axis.
C. Minimum at the surface of the conductor - FALSE. The field is maximum at the surface.
D. Minimum at the axis of the conductor - TRUE. The field is zero at $r = 0$, making it the minimum.
E. Same at all points in the cross-section - FALSE. The field varies from 0 at the axis to maximum at the surface.
Only D is correct.

questions.q:
Three long straight wires carrying current are arranged mutually parallel as shown in the figure. The force experienced by 15 cm length of wire $Q$ is $\_\_\_\_$.

($\mu_{\mathrm{o}}=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~T}. \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{A}$)
questions.solution:
The force per unit length between parallel wires is $F/L = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$.
Force on Q from P (opposite currents, repulsive towards R): $\frac{F_{QP}}{L} = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 3 \times 1}{2\pi \times 0.03} = 2 \times 10^{-5}$ N/m.
Force on Q from R (same currents, attractive towards R): $\frac{F_{QR}}{L} = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1 \times 2}{2\pi \times 0.02} = 2 \times 10^{-5}$ N/m.
Total force per unit length towards R: $4 \times 10^{-5}$ N/m.
For 0.15 m length: $F = 4 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.15 = 6 \times 10^{-6}$ N towards R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop of radius $R$ is $16 \mu \mathrm{~T}$. The magnetic field at a distance $x=\sqrt{3} R$ on its axis from the centre is $\_\_\_\_$\mu \mathrm{T}$.
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at the center of a circular loop is $B_{center} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R} = 16\mu$ T.
On the axis at distance $x$ from center: $B(x) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$.
At $x = \sqrt{3}R$: $B(\sqrt{3}R) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + 3R^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(4R^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{16R}$.
The ratio: $\frac{B(\sqrt{3}R)}{B_{center}} = \frac{1/16R}{1/2R} = \frac{1}{8}$.
Therefore: $B(\sqrt{3}R) = \frac{1}{8} \times 16\mu = 2\mu$ T.

questions.q: Two identical circular loops $P$ and $Q$ each of radius $r$ are lying in parallel planes such that they have common axis. The current through $P$ and $Q$ are $I$ and $4 I$ respectively in clockwise direction as seen from $O$. The net magnetic field at $O$ is:
questions.solution:
Two identical circular loops P and Q, each of radius $r$, are separated by distance $r$ along their common axis. Current in P is $I$ and in Q is $4I$ (both clockwise as seen from O).
Point O is at the midpoint. The magnetic fields from each loop at O:
$B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + R^2)^{3/2}}$ (from P, pointing toward Q)
$B_2 = \frac{4\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + R^2)^{3/2}}$ (from Q, pointing toward P)
$B_{net} = B_2 - B_1 = \frac{3\mu_0 I R^2}{2(2R^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{3\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}R}$
Direction: towards Q.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A short bar magnet placed with its axis at $30^{\circ}$ with an external field of 800 Gauss, experiences a torque of $0.016 \mathrm{~N}. \mathrm{m}$. The work done in moving it from most stable to most unstable position is $\alpha \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~J}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
For a magnetic dipole in an external field, torque is $\tau = mB\sin\theta$
At 30°: $0.016 = m \times 0.08 \times \sin 30°$
$0.016 = m \times 0.08 \times 0.5$
$m = 0.4$ A·m$^2$
Work done from most stable (aligned, 0°) to most unstable (anti-aligned, 180°) position equals the change in potential energy:
$W = U_0° - U_{180°} = -mB\cos 0° - (-mB\cos 180°) = -mB - mB = 2mB$
$W = 2 \times 0.4 \times 0.08 = 0.064$ J $= 64 \times 10^{-3}$ J
Therefore, $\alpha = 64$

questions.q:
The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side $4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm}$ is 2 A. The magnetic field at its centroid is $\alpha \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
(Given : $\mu_{\mathrm{o}}=4 \pi \times 10^{-7}$ SI units)
questions.solution:
For an equilateral triangle of side $a$, the distance of the centroid from any side is $r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{3}}$.
Given side $a = 4\sqrt{3}$ cm $= 4\sqrt{3} \times 10^{-2}$ m.
So, $r = \frac{4\sqrt{3} \times 10^{-2}}{2\sqrt{3}} = 2 \times 10^{-2}$ m.
The magnetic field at the centroid due to one side of the triangle is $B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (\sin \theta_1 + \sin \theta_2)$.
For an equilateral triangle, $\theta_1 = \theta_2 = 60^\circ$.
$B_1 = \frac{10^{-7} \times 2}{2 \times 10^{-2}} (\sin 60^\circ + \sin 60^\circ) = 10^{-5} \times (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) = \sqrt{3} \times 10^{-5}$ T.
The total magnetic field at the centroid due to all three sides is $B = 3B_1 = 3\sqrt{3} \times 10^{-5}$ T.
Comparing with $B = \alpha \times 10^{-5}$ T, we get $\alpha = 3\sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current carrying solenoid is placed vertically and a particle of mass $m$ with charge $Q$ is released from rest. The particle moves along the axis of solenoid. If $g$ is acceleration due to gravity then the acceleration (a) of the charged particle will satisfy :
questions.solution:
Inside a solenoid, magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is uniform and parallel to the axis.
Particle moves along the axis, so velocity $\vec{v}$ is parallel to $\vec{B}$.
Magnetic force $\vec{F} = Q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) = 0$ (since $\vec{v} \parallel \vec{B}$)
Only gravity acts on the particle.
Acceleration $a = g$

questions.q:
Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths $\left(B_1\right.$ and B_2), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass m and charge q , at the interface at an instant, moves into the region 2 with velocityv$ and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface?

(Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and $B_2 \gt B_1$)$
questions.solution:
As $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}$ is $\perp$ to $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$, so charge particle will move in circular path, whose radius is given by
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}}$

Starting point $\rightarrow \mathrm{A}$
Ending point $\rightarrow \mathrm{C}$
$\therefore$ Net displacement $=\mathrm{AC}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AC}=\mathrm{CD}-\mathrm{AD} \\ & \mathrm{AC}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_1}-\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_2} \\ & \mathrm{AC}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_1}\left[1-\frac{\mathrm{B}_1}{\mathrm{~B}_2}\right]\end{aligned}$

Amount of work, required to rotate the coil through $90^{\circ}$ from its initial orientation such that $\vec{M}$ becomes perpendicular to $\vec{B}$, is ______ $\mu \mathrm{J}$.
questions.solution:
We know
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{W}_{\text{ext }} & =\Delta \mathrm{U}+\Delta \mathrm{KE} \quad(\text{ P.E. }=-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}) \\
& =-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{f}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{i}}+0 \\
& =-\mathrm{MB} \cos 90+\mathrm{MB} \cos 0 \\
& =\mathrm{MB} \\
& =\mathrm{NIAB} \\
& =200 \times 100 \times 10^{-6} \times \frac{5}{2} \times 10^{-4} \times 1=5 \mu \mathrm{J}
\end{aligned}$

options: the electron will continue to move with uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid.
the electron will be accelerated along the axis.
the electron path will be circular about the axis.
the electron will experience a force at $45^{\circ}$ to the axis and execute a helical path.
questions.solution: Since $\vec{v} \| \vec{B}$ so force on electron due to magnetic field is zero. So it will move along axis with uniform velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field existing in a region is given by $\vec{B}=0.2(1+2 x) \hat{k} \mathrm{~T}$. A square loop of edge $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ carrying 0.5 A current is placed in $x-y$ plane with its edges parallel to the $x-y$ axes, as shown in figure. The magnitude of the net magnetic force experienced by the loop is_____ $\mathrm{mN}$.
questions.solution:
Force on segment parallel to $\mathrm{x}$-axis will cancel each other. Hence $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}$ will be due to portion parallel to $y$-axis.
$\begin{aligned}
& F=0.5 \times 0.5 \times 6 \times 0.2-0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.2 \times 5 \\
& =0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.2 \\
& =0.25 \times 0.2 \\
& =50 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~N} \\
& =50 \mathrm{mN}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A moving coil galvanometer has $100$ turns and each turn has an area of $2 . 0{cm}^{2} .$ The magnetic field produced by the magnet is $0 . 01T$ and the deflection in the coil is $0 . 05$ radian when a current of $10mA$ is passed through it. The torsional constant of the suspension wire is $x \times {10}^{- 5}N - m / rad .$ The value of $x$ is ______ .
questions.solution:
Torque produced in a moving coil galvanometer is, $τ = BINAsinϕ$.

Let torsional constant of the suspension wire be $C$, then $C\theta = BINAsin90 °$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{BINA}{\theta} = \dfrac{0 . 01 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 100 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 4}}{0 . 05}$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 5}N - m / rad .$

Therefore, $x = 4$.

Therefore, $x = 4$.

questions.q: A regular polygon of $6$ sides is formed by bending a wire of length $4\pi$ meter. If an electric current of $4\pi\sqrt{3}A$ is flowing through the sides of the polygon, the magnetic field at the centre of the polygon would be $x \times {10}^{- 7}T .$ The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Direction of magnetic field due to all six sides will be in the same direction, therefore we can write 

$B = 6\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pir}\right)\left(sin30 ° + sin30 °\right)$, where $r =$distance of the sides from the centre.

$= 6\dfrac{{10}^{- 7} \times 4\pi\sqrt{3}}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} \times \sqrt{3}\right)}$

$= 72 \times {10}^{- 7}T$

Hence, $x = 72$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two circular coils $P$ and $Q$ of $100$ turns each have same radius of $\picm$. The currents in $P$ and $R$ are $1A$ and $2A$ respectively. $P$ and $Q$ are placed with their planes mutually perpendicular with their centers coincide. The resultant magnetic field induction at the center of the coils is $\sqrt{x}mT$, where $x =$ ______. [Use ${\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}Tm{A}^{- 1}$]
questions.solution:
Consider two coils as shown below:

Magnetic field due to P, ${B}_{P} = N\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{1}}{2r}\right) = 100 \times \dfrac{{\mu}_{0} \times 1}{2\left(\pi \times {10}^{- 2}\right)} = 2 \times {10}^{- 3}T$

Magnetic field due to Q, 

${B}_{Q} = N\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{2}}{2r}\right) = 100 \times \dfrac{{\mu}_{0} \times 2}{2\pi \times {10}^{- 2}} = 4 \times {10}^{- 3}T$

Therefore, ${B}_{net} = \sqrt{{B}_{P}^{2} + {B}_{Q}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{20}mT$

Hence, $x = 20$

questions.q: A uniform magnetic field of $2 \times {10}^{- 3}T$ acts along positive Y-direction. A rectangular loop of sides $20cm$  and $10cm$ with current of $5A$ is in Y-Z plane. The current is in anticlockwise sense with reference to negative X axis. Magnitude and direction of the torque is :
questions.solution:
Magnetic moment is given by, $\overset{\to}{M} = i\overset{\to}{A}$

$= 5 \times \left(0 . 2\right) \times \left(0 . 1\right)\left(- \overset{^}{i}\right)$

$= 0 . 1\left(- \overset{^}{i}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{M} \times \overset{\to}{B} = 0 .1 \left(- \overset{^}{i}\right) \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)\left(\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 4}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)Nm$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron moves through a uniform magnetic field $\overset{\to}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + 2{B}_{0}\overset{^}{j}T$. At a particular instant of time, the velocity of electron is $\overset{\to}{u} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}m{s}^{- 1}$. If the magnetic force acting on electron is $\overset{\to}{F} = 5e\overset{^}{k}N$, where $e$ is the charge of electron, then the value of ${B}_{0}$ is ____ $T$.
questions.solution:
Force acting on a charged particle under the magnetic field is given by, $\overset{\to}{F} = q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$.

$⇒ 5e\overset{⏜}{k} = e\left(3\overset{⏜}{i} + 5\overset{⏜}{j}\right) \times \left({B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{i} + 2{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{j}\right)$

$⇒ 5e\overset{⏜}{k} = e\left(6{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{k} - 5{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{k}\right)$

$⇒ {B}_{0} = 5T$

questions.q: A rigid wire consists of a semicircular portion of radius $R$ and two straight sections. The wire is partially immerged in a perpendicular magnetic field $B = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$ as shown in figure. The magnetic force on the wire if it has a current $i$ is :
questions.solution:
Direction of magnetic field is in $+ \overset{^}{k}$

Force acting on wire is given by, $\overset{\to}{F} = i\left(\overset{\to}{l} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$

As, $l = 2R$, we get

$⇒ \overset{\to}{F} = - 2iRB\overset{^}{j}$

questions.q: The current of $5A$ flows in a square loop of sides $1m$ is placed in air. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is $X\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 7}T$. The value of $X$ is _________.
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the square loop is given by,

$B = 4\left[\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pid}\left(sin45 ° + sin45 °\right)\right]$, where $d$ is perpendicular distance of the centre to one of its sides.

$⇒ B = 4 \times \dfrac{{\mu}_{0} \times 5}{4\pi \times \dfrac{1}{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 5 \times 2 \times \sqrt{2}$

$= 40\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 7}T$

questions.q: The horizontal component of earth's magnetic field at a place is $3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}T$. A very long straight conductor carrying current of $\sqrt{2}A$ in the direction from South east to North West is placed. The force per unit length experienced by the conductor is ________$\times {10}^{- 6}N{m}^{- 1}$.

Horizontal component of magnetic field, ${B}_{H} = 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}T$

$= 35 \times {10}^{- 6}N{m}^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two insulated circular loop $A$ and $B$ radius $a$ carrying a current of $I$ in the anti clockwise direction as shown in figure. The magnitude of the magnetic induction at the centre will be:
questions.solution:
Right hand thumb rule states that, “If you imagine holding a current carrying wire in your right-hand with your thumb pointing towards the direction of electric current flow then the direction in which your fingers curl, gives the direction of lines of force of the magnetic field”. In this case, direciton of magnetic field at the centre for both wires is as shown below.

Magnetic field due to a circular wire is given by, ${B}_{A} = {B}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2a}$

As both magnetic field lines at centre are perpendicular, therefore

$∵ {B}_{net} = \sqrt{{\left({B}_{A}\right)}^{2} + {\left({B}_{B}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{\mu}_{0}I}{2a} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{\sqrt{2}a}$

questions.q: A charge of $4 . 0\muC$ is moving with a velocity of $4 . 0 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}$ along the positive $y$-axis under a magnetic field $B$ of strength $( 2\overset{^}{k} ) T$. The force acting on the charge is $x\overset{^}{i}N$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Given:

$q = 4\muC, \overset{\to}{v} = 4 \times {10}^{6}\overset{^}{j}m{s}^{- 1}$ and $\overset{\to}{B} = 2\overset{^}{k}T$

Force acting on charged particle, $\overset{\to}{F} = q ( \overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B} )$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 6}\left(4 \times {10}^{6}\overset{^}{j} \times 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 8 \times {10}^{6}\overset{^}{i}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{F} = 32\overset{^}{i}N$

$⇒ x = 32$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two particles $X$ and $Y$ having equal charges are being accelerated through the same potential difference. Thereafter, they enter normally in a region of uniform magnetic field and describes circular paths of radii ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ respectively. The mass ratio of $X$ and $Y$ is :
questions.solution:
Energy gained due to potential difference by charged particle:

$KE = qV$

Relation between momentum & kinetic energy:

$p = \sqrt{2m\left(KE\right)}$

Now, radius of the circular path under magnetic field will be given by, 

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{p}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2m ( KE )}}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB}$

Therefore,

$R ∝ \sqrt{m} ⇒ m ∝ {R}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = {\left(\dfrac{{R}_{1}}{{R}_{2}}\right)}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis situated at a distance of $20cm$ from its center is $1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}Tm$. The magnetic moment of the dipole is _______ $A{m}^{2}$. (Given : $\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi} = {10}^{- 7}Tm{A}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole can be written as

$V = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{{r}^{2}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required magnetic moment of the dipole.

$1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5} = {10}^{- 7} \times \dfrac{M}{{\left(20 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2}} ⇒ M = \dfrac{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 20 \times 20 \times {10}^{- 4}}{{10}^{- 7}} ⇒ M = 1 . 5 \times 4 = 6A{m}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a wire loop formed by two semicircular wires of radii ${R}_{1} = 2\pim$ and ${R}_{2} = 4\pim$ carrying current $I = 4A$ as per figure given below is $\alpha \times {10}^{- 7}T$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____. (Centre $O$ is common for all segments)
questions.solution:
From the figure, it is evident that the magnetic field at $O$ due to the straight portion of the loop is zero, only the contributions from the circular parts survive.

Also, the direction of the magnetic field due to the circular loops can be determined by the right-hand corkscrew rule.

Hence, the net magnetic field at $O$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}B & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2{R}_{2}}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2\pi}\right) ⊗ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2{R}_{1}}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2\pi}\right) ⊗ \\ & = & \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4{R}_{2}} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4{R}_{1}}\right) ⊗ \\ & = & \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 4}{4 \times 4\pi} + \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 4}{4 \times 2\pi} ⊗ T \\ & = & 3 \times {10}^{- 7} ⊗ T\end{cases}$

Hence, $\alpha = 3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two long, straight wires carry equal currents in opposite directions as shown in figure. The separation between the wires is $5 . 0cm$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a point $P$ midway between the wires is $_____\muT$. (Given: ${\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}Tm{A}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
The direction of the magnetic field at the observation point due to the current carrying conductor is determined by the right-hand cork screw rule.

From the given diagram, it is clear that as the conductors carry current in the mutually opposite direction, the direction of the magnetic fields produced by them at point $P$ will be the same.

Hence, the required magnetic field at $P$ due to the conductors can be calculated as follows:

questions.q:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If $\overset{ o}{E}$ and $\overset{ o}{B}$ represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, then the region of space may have :
(A) $E = 0, B = 0$; (B) $E = 0, B e 0$; (C) $E e 0, B = 0$; (D) $E e 0, B e 0$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Net force on proton inside an electric and a magnetic field is given by

$\overset{ o}{F}e + \overset{ o}{F}m = q\overset{ o}{E} + q\left(\overset{ o}{v} imes \overset{ o}{B} ight) . . . \left(1 ight)$

If both $\overset{ o}{E}$ and $\overset{ o}{B}$ are zero, then $\overset{ o}{F}e$ and $\overset{ o}{F}m$ both are zero. Hence, velocity may remain constant. Therefore, option (A) is correct.

If $E = 0, B e 0$, but velocity is parallel or antiparallel to the magnetic field, then also $\overset{ o}{F}e$ and $\overset{ o}{F}m$ both are zero. Hence, option (B) is also correct.

If $E e 0, B e 0$, but $\overset{ o}{F}e + \overset{ o}{F}m = 0$, then also velocity may remain constant. Thus, option (D) is also correct.

questions.q: An electron in a hydrogen atom revolves around its nucleus with a speed of $6 . 76 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{– 1}$ in an orbit of radius $0 . 52Å$. The magnetic field produced at the nucleus of the hydrogen atom is _______ $T$.
questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the electron is given by

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}qvsin90 °}{4\pi{r}^{2}}$

The given data is

$v = 6 . 76 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}r = 0 . 52 \times {10}^{- 10}m$

Thus, the magnetic field is

$B = \dfrac{{10}^{- 7} \times \left(1 . 6 \times \times {10}^{- 19}\right) \times \left(6 . 76 \times {10}^{6}\right)}{0 . 52 \times 0 . 52 \times {10}^{- 20}} = 40T$

questions.q:
An electron is moving along the positive x-axis. If uniform magnetic field is applied parallel to the negative z-axis, then

A.The electron will experience magnetic force along positive y-axis

B.The electron will experience magnetic force along negative y-axis

C.The electron will not experience any force in magnetic field

D.The electron will continue to move along the positive x-axis

E.The electron will move along circular path in magnetic field

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.solution:
The Lorentz force is given by

$\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}$

$= - e\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}$

So, $\overset{^}{F} = \overset{^}{i} \times \overset{^}{k} = - \overset{^}{j}$.

$\overset{\to}{F}is\text{along} - y\text{axis}$

As the magnetic field is perpendicular to the velocity, motion would be circular.

questions.q: A straight wire AB of mass $40g$ and length $50cm$ is suspended by a pair of flexible leads in uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0 . 40T$ as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the current required in the wire to remove the tension in the supporting leads is _____ $A$. (Take $\leftg = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right)$.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic force on the conductor is given by

${F}_{B} = ILB . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the gravitational force on the conductor is given by

${F}_{G} = mg . . . \left(2\right)$

Equate both the equations and simplify to obtain the required current through the conductor.

$\begin{cases}ILB & = & mg \\ & ⇒ & I = \dfrac{mg}{LB} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required current through the conductor.

$\begin{cases}I & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{40}{1000}kg \times 10m{s}^{- 2}}{0 . 5m \times 0 . 40T} \\ & = & 2A\end{cases}$

(A) The electron will experience magnetic force along the axis of the solenoid.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer is doubled then the current sensitivity becomes double.

Statement II: Increasing current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer by only increasing the number of turns in the coil will also increase its voltage sensitivity in the same ratio

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
questions.solution:
For a moving coil galvanometer,

$\left(NiAB\right) = k\theta$

The current sensitivity is given by

${S}_{i} = \dfrac{NAB}{k}$

So, if $N$ is doubled then, the current sensitivity is also doubled.

The voltage is given by

$V = \left(\dfrac{BNA}{Rk}\right)\theta$

The voltage sensitivity is given by

${S}_{v} = \left(\dfrac{NAB}{kR}\right)$

As, $N$ is increased, $R$ also increases. So, the voltage sensitivity does not change as $\dfrac{N}{R}$ remains constant.

questions.q: The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying coil of radius $r$ to the magnetic field at distance $r$ from the centre of coil on its axis is $\sqrt{x}: 1$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field at any axial point situated at a distance $x$ from the centre of a circular current carrying conductor of radius $r$ can be written as

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{r}^{2}}{2{\left({r}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)$}^{3 / 2}} . . . $\left(1\right)$

Substitute $0$ for $x$ in equation (1) to calculate the magnetic field $\left({B}_{c}\right)$ at the centre of the conductor.

$\begin{cases}{B}_{c} & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{r}^{2}}{2{\left({r}^{2} + {0}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}} \\ & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{r}^{2}}{2{r}^{3}} \\ & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2r} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute $r$ for $x$ in equation (1) to calculate the magnetic field $\left({B}_{r}\right)$ at the given distance from the centre of the conductor.

$\begin{cases}{B}_{r} & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{r}^{2}}{2{\left({r}^{2} + {r}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}} \\ & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{r}^{2}}{4\sqrt{2}{r}^{3}} \\ & = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\sqrt{2}r} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) to calculate the required ratio of the magnetic fields.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{B}_{c}}{{B}_{r}} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2r}}{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\sqrt{2}r}} \\ & = & 2\sqrt{2} \\ & = & \sqrt{8}\end{cases}

$

questions.q: A charge particle moving in magnetic field $B,$ has the components of velocity along $B$ as well as perpendicular to $B$. The path of the charge particle will be
options: helical path with the axis perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field $B$
helical path with the axis along magnetic field $B$
straight along the direction of magnetic field $B$
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the radius of the path followed by the charged particle under an external magnetic field can be written as

$r = \dfrac{mv}{Bq} . . . \left(1\right)$

The perpendicular component of velocity results in circular motion, while the parallel component results in linear motion. Hence, the path of the charged particle is helical in nature, the axis of which lies along the direction of the magnetic field.

questions.q: The magnetic intensity at the centre of a long current carrying solenoid is found to be $1 . 6 \times {10}^{3}A{m}^{- 1}$. If the number of turns is $8$ per $cm$, then the current flowing through the solenoid is $______A .$
questions.solution:
The magnetic intensity $H$ is defined as the product of the number of turns per unit length in a coil $n$ and the current that it carries$I$.

The magnetic field of a solenoid is given by $B = {\mu}_{0}ni$

$H = \dfrac{B}{{\mu}_{0}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}ni}{{\mu}_{0}} ⇒ H = ni . . . ( i )$

The given data is

$H = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{3}A{m}^{- 1}$

$n = 8$ per $cm$

Substituting the values in equation (i)

$⇒ 1 . 6 \times 1000 = \dfrac{8}{\dfrac{1}{100}} \times i$

$⇒ i = 2A$

questions.q: A proton with a kinetic energy of $2 . 0eV$ moves into a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \times {10}^{- 3}T$. The angle between the direction of magnetic field and velocity of proton is ${60}^{o}$. The pitch of the helical path taken by the proton is ____ $cm$. (Take, mass of proton $= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27}kg$ and charge on proton $= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$).
questions.solution:
The given data is

$K . E = 2eV$

$B = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \times {10}^{- 3}T$

$\theta = {60}^{o}$

The pitch of the proton is given by

$P = \dfrac{2\pim}{qB} \times vcos\theta . . . ( i )$

By using

$K = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} ⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2K}{m}}$

Substituting the values in equation (i)

$= \dfrac{2\pi \times \sqrt{2mKE} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times \pi \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times \sqrt{2 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27} \times 2 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}} \times {10}^{3}}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}$

$= 2 \times 2 \times {10}^{– 1} = 0 . 4m$

questions.q: A long straight wire of circular cross-section (radius $a$) is carrying steady current $I .$ The current $I$ is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The magnetic field is

questions.solution:

${B}_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}J{a}^{2}}{2r} . . . ( 2 )$

From equation (1), it can be concluded that the magnetic field is directly proportional to the radial distance inside the wire, whereas from equation (2), it can be concluded that the magnetic field is inversely proportional to the radial distance outside the wire.

(Take $\pi = 3 . 14$)
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field $\left(B\right)$ at the centre of a current carrying circular loop is given by

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R} . . . ( 1 )$

where, ${\mu}_{0}$ is the permeability of free space, $i$ is the current and $R$ is the radius of the loop.

${B}_{V}, {B}_{H}$ are the magnetic field due to the vertical and the horizontal loop, which by magnitude are equal.

The resultant magnetic field $\left({B}_{net}\right)$ at the centre is, then, given by

${B}_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{{B}^{2} + {B}^{2}} = \sqrt{2}B = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times \sqrt{2}}{2 \times 0 . 2}$

$= 628 \times {10}^{- 8}T$

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a long straight conductor with semicircular arc of radius $\dfrac{\pi}{10}m$ is carrying current $I = 3A$. The magnitude of the magnetic field. at the center $O$ of the arc is: (The permeability of the vacuum $= 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}{NA}^{- 2}$ )
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field $\left({B}_{C}\right)$ produced at the centre of a circular current carrying conductor is given by

${B}_{C} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{o}I}{4\pir}\theta . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where, ${\mu}_{0}$ is the permeability of free space, $I$ is the current through the conductor, $r$ is the radius of the circular conductor and $\theta$ is the angle subtended by the arc at the centre.

From the given figure, it is clear that the arc of the conductor makes an angle $\pi$ at its centre.

Substitute the known values of the parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required magnetic field.

$\begin{cases}{B}_{C} & = & \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}N{A}^{- 2} \times 3A}{4 \times \pi \times \dfrac{\pi}{10}m} \times \pi \\ & = & 3 \times {10}^{- 6}T \times \dfrac{{10}^{6}\mu T}{1T} \\ & = & 3\mu T\end{cases}$

questions.q: Find the magnetic field at the point P in figure. The curved portion is a semicircle connected to two long straight wires.
questions.solution:
Magnitude of magnetic field due to semi-infinite portion of wire AB at point C is

${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\pir}$

Magnitude of magnetic field due to semicircular arc BD at point C is

${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4r}$

Magnitude of magnetic field due to semi-infinite portion DE at point C is 0.

Using right-hand rule, it can be seen that directions of $\overset{\to}{{B}_{1}}$ and $\overset{\to}{{B}_{2}}$ are both outwards from the plane.

Therefore, the magnitude of net magnetic field at point C is

$B = {B}_{1} + {B}_{2}$

$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2r}\left[\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\right]$

questions.q: A charge particle of $2\mu C$ accelerated by a potential difference of $100V$ enters a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $4mT$ at right angle to the direction of field. The charge particle completes semicircle of radius $3cm$ inside magnetic field. The mass of the charge particle is ______ $\times {10}^{- 18}kg$.
questions.solution:
As we know, radius of the circular path is given by,

$r = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 \times m \times qV}}{qB}$

$⇒ {r}^{2} = \dfrac{2mV}{q{B}^{2}}$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{{r}^{2}q{B}^{2}}{2V} = \dfrac{{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2} \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 6}\right) \times {\left(4 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 100} = 144 \times {10}^{- 18}kg$

questions.q: A long conducting wire having a current $I$ flowing through it, is bent into a circular coil of $N$ turns. Then it is bent into a circular coil of $n$ turns. The magnetic field is calculated at the centre of coils in both the cases. The ratio of the magnetic field in first case to that of second case is:
questions.solution:
As in both cases, length of the wire will remain the same, therefore

$l = \left(2\piR\right)N = \left(2\pir\right)n ⇒ \dfrac{R}{r} = \dfrac{n}{N}$

Now magnetic field due to single circular coil is given by, $B = \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2r}\right)$.

Therefore, required ratio of total magnetic field wil be,

$\dfrac{{B}_{1}}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{N\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2R}\right)}{n\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2r}\right)} = \left(\dfrac{{N}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}\right)$

questions.q: A bar magnet with a magnetic moment $5 . 0A{m}^{2}$ is placed in parallel position relative to a magnetic field of $0 . 4T$. The amount of required work done in turning the magnet form parallel to antiparallel position relative to the field direction is ________.
questions.solution:
For a bar magnet, the work done in turning from parallel to antiparallel position relative to the field direction is

$W = MB\left(cos{\theta}_{1} - cos{\theta}_{2}\right)$, here, ${\theta}_{1} = 0 ° and{\theta}_{1} = 180 °$.

$W = - MBcos180 ° \left(- mBcos0 °\right)$

$W = 2MB = 2 \times 5 \times 0 . 4 = 4J$

A rod with circular cross-section area $2{cm}^{2}$ and length $40cm$ is wound uniformly with $400$ turns of an insulated wire. If a current of $0 . 4A$ flows in the wire windings, the total magnetic flux produced inside windings is $4\pi \times {10}^{- 6}Wb$. The relative permeability of the rod is

(Given : Permeability of vacuum ${\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}N{A}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Magnetic flux is given by $ϕ = NBA$, here, $N$ is number of turns, $B$ is magnetic field and $A$ is area.

Given here, $ϕ = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 6}Wb, A = 2{cm}^{2}, N = 400, I = 0 . 4A$.

Putting the values,

$ϕ = 400 \times \left({\mu}_{r}{\mu}_{0}nI\right) \times A$

$⇒ 4\pi \times {10}^{- 6} = 400\left[{\mu}_{r} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times \dfrac{400}{0 . 4} \times 0 . 4\right] \times 2 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ {\mu}_{r} = 125$

A massless square loop, of wire of resistance $10Ω$, supporting a mass of $1g$, hangs vertically with one of its sides in a uniform magnetic field of ${10}^{3}G$, directed outwards in the shaded region. A dc voltage $V$ is applied to the loop. For what value of $V$, the magnetic force will exactly balance the weight of the supporting mass of $1g$?

(If sides of the loop $= 10cm, g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)

.
questions.solution:
For balancing of force,

Magnetic force $\left({F}_{m}\right) =$weight of supporting mass $\left(mg\right)$.

$∴ ILB = mg$

$∴ \left(\dfrac{V}{R}\right)LB = mg\left(∵ \text{From Ohm's law}, I = \dfrac{V}{R}\right)$

$∴ V = \dfrac{mgR}{LB}$

$= \dfrac{\left(1 \times {10}^{- 3}kg\right)\left(10m{s}^{- 2}\right)\left(10Ω\right)}{\left(0 . 1m\right)\left({10}^{3} \times {10}^{- 4}T\right)} = 10V$

questions.q: The electric current in a circular coil of four turns produces a magnetic induction $32T$ at its centre. The coil is unwound and is rewound into a circular coil of single turn, the magnetic induction at the centre of the coil by the same current will be :
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the coil is given by, $B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}$.

Now in the first case:

$B = 4\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}\right)$

and for the second case:

$B ' = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R '}$.

As the length of the wire will remain same, therefore

$2\piR ' = 4\left(2\piR\right) ⇒ R ' = 4R$

Hence, required ratio will be

$\dfrac{B '}{B} = \dfrac{R}{4{R}^{'}} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

$⇒ B ' = 2T$

Now force acting on the side of the square loop, $F = Bil = 40 \times 0 . 01 \times 0 . 05$

$⇒ F = 0 . 02N$

Therefore, work done

$W = Fl = 0 . 02 \times l = 0 . 02 \times 0 . 05$

$⇒ W = 1 \times {10}^{- 3}J$

questions.q: For a moving coil galvanometer, the deflection in the coil is $0 . 05rad$ when a current of $10mA$ is passed through it. If the torsional constant of suspension wire is $4 . 0 \times {10}^{– 5}Nm{rad}^{- 1}$, the magnetic field is $0 . 01T$ and the number of turns in the coil is $200$, the area of each turn (in ${cm}^{2}$ ) is :
questions.solution:
Given: $\theta = 0 . 05rad, I = 10mA, K = 4 \times {10}^{- 5}Nm{rad}^{- 1}, B = 0 . 01T, N = 200$

The torsional constant of a wire used in a moving coil galvanometer is given by

$K = \dfrac{NIAB}{\theta}$, where, $A$ is area of each turn

So, $A = \dfrac{K\theta}{NIB} = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 0 . 05}{200 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 01}$

Thus, $A = {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2} = 1{cm}^{2}$

$K = \dfrac{NIAB}{\theta}$, where, $A$ is area of each turn

So, $A = \dfrac{K\theta}{NIB} = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 0 . 05}{200 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 01}$

Thus, $A = {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2} = 1{cm}^{2}$

questions.q: Two long parallel wires carrying currents $8A$ and $15A$ in opposite directions are placed at a distance of $7cm$ from each other. A point $P$ is at equidistant from both the wires such that the lines joining the point $P$ to the wires are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of magnetic field at $P$ is ______ $\times {10}^{- 6}T$. (Given: $\sqrt{2} = 1 . 4$)
questions.solution:
Here, the magnetic fields produced by the two wires will be perpendicular to one another.

Magnetic field due to wire carrying current $8A$ is ${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{1}}{2\pid}$

and magnetic field due to wire carrying current $15A$ is ${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$

The net magnetic field is

${B}_{net} = \sqrt{{B}_{1}^{2} + {B}_{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{2\pid}\sqrt{{i}_{1}^{2} + {i}_{2}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}}{2\pi \times \left(\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \times {10}^{- 2}} \times \sqrt{{8}^{2} + {15}^{2}}\left(d = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}}cm\right)$

$= 68 \times {10}^{- 6}T$.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II

List – I
(Current configuration)		 List – II
(Magnetic field at point $O$)
A I. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pir} [ \pi + 2 ]$
B II. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4}\dfrac{I}{r}$
C III. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2\pir} [ \pi - 1 ]$
D IV. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pir} [ \pi + 1 ]$

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.solution:
(A)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and due to loop $bcd$.

So, ${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$ (directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi )$ (in the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi ) - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{2\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi - 1 )$ (III)

(B)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and semicircular arc $bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$ (directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$ (out of the plane)

Thus, net magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi ) + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 2 )$ (I)

(C)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and due to loop $bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$ (directed in the plane)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$ (in the plane)

${B}_{de} = 0$ (passing through the axis)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 1 )$ (IV)

(D)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and due to loop $bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = 0 = {B}_{de}$ (passing through the axis)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$ (out of the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4r}$ (II).

A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.q: A solenoid of $1200$ turns is wound uniformly in a single layer on a glass tube $2m$ long and $0 . 2m$ in diameter. The magnetic intensity at the center of the solenoid when a current of $2A$ flows through it is:
questions.solution:
Given,

Number of turns per metre $n = \dfrac{1200}{2}$

$l = 2m, d = 0 . 2m\text{and}I = 2A$

Magnetic field at centre inside the solenoid is given by $B = {\mu}_{0}nI$, where, ${\mu}_{0}$ is the permeability constant.

Magnetic intensity is related to magnetic field by

$H = \dfrac{B}{{\mu}_{0}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}nI}{{\mu}_{0}} = nI = \left(\dfrac{1200}{2}\right) ( 2 )$

$⇒ H = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{3}A{m}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
A long solenoid is formed by winding $70$ turns ${cm}^{- 1}$ . If $2 . 0A$ current flows, then the magnetic field produced inside the solenoid is ______________.

$( {µ}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{– 7}Tm{A}^{– 1} )$
questions.solution:
Magnetic field inside solenoid $= {\mu}_{o}ni$

where $n =$ Number of turns per unit length

$n = 7000$ turns/m

${B}_{\text{solenoid}} = {\mu}_{o}ni = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 7000 \times 2$

$= 8 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times {10}^{- 6} \times 7 \times 100$

$= 176 \times {10}^{- 4}T$

questions.q: A single turn current loop in the shape of a right angle triangle with sides $5cm, 12cm, 13cm$ is carrying a current of $2A$. The loop is in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0 . 75T$ whose direction is parallel to the current in the $13cm$ side of the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic force on the $5cm$ side will be $\dfrac{x}{130}N$. The value of $x$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Here, $B = 0 . 75T$

The magnitude of magnetic force on the $5cm$ side is ${F}_{AB} = i \times \left({l}_{AB}\right)Bsin\theta\left(\text{angle between}AC \text{ and } AB\right)$

$= 2 \times \left(\dfrac{5}{100}\right) \times 0 . 75 \times \dfrac{12}{13}$

$= \dfrac{9}{130}N$

Hence, the value of $x = 9$.

questions.q: Two long straight wires $P$ and $Q$ carrying equal current $10A$ each were kept parallel to each other at $5cm$ distance. Magnitude of magnetic force experienced by $10cm$ length of wire $P$ is ${F}_{1}$. If distance between wires is halved and currents on them are doubled, force ${F}_{2}$ on $10cm$ length of wire $P$ will be:
questions.solution:
As we know, force per unit length between two parallel straight wires is given by, $F = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{1}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$.

Therefore, required ratio

$\dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0} ( 10{)}^{2}}{2\pi ( 5 \times {10}^{- 2} )}}{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0} ( 20{)}^{2}}{2\pi\left(\dfrac{5}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$⇒ {F}_{2} = 8{F}_{1}$

questions.q: A circular loop of radius $R$ is carrying current $iA$. The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of circular loop and at a distance $R$ from the center of the loop on its axis is :
questions.solution:
The magnitude of magnetic field at the centre of loop is

${B}_{\text{1}} = {B}_{\text{centre}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{∘}i}{2R} \ldots \left(1\right)$

The magnitude of magnetic field at a point at a distance $x$ from the centre along axis of loop is

${B}_{\text{axis}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{∘}i{R}^{2}}{2{\left({R}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}$

${B}_{\text{2}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{∘}i{R}^{2}}{2\left(2\dfrac{3}{2}\right){R}^{3}} \ldots \left(2\right)$( \text{since}x = R )$

Dividing equation 1 by equation 2, we get

$\dfrac{{B}_{1}}{{B}_{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}: 1$

questions.q:
A wire $X$ of length $50cm$ carrying a current of $2A$ is placed parallel to a long wire $Y$ of length $5m$. The wire $Y$ carries a current of $3A$. The distance between two wires is $5cm$ and currents flow in the same direction. The force acting on the wire $Y$ is :

​​​​​​​
questions.solution:
An attractive force will act normal to $X$ towards $Y$ because the direction of the currents in the wires is the same.

Force exerted on length $l$ due to the magnetic field is given as $F = {F}_{XY} = {F}_{YX} = {I}_{1}{l}_{1}{B}_{12}$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pir}{l}_{1}$

Given here, ${I}_{1} = 2A, {I}_{2} = 3A, {l}_{1} = 5m, r = 5cm$.

Putting the values, we have

$F = \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 2 \times 3}{2\pi \times 5 \times {10}^{- 2}} \times 50 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 5}N$ directed towards wire $X$.

questions.q: A wire of length $314cm$ carrying current of $14A$ is bent to form a circle. The magnetic moment of the coil is $A - {m}^{2}$. [Given $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.solution:
Length of the wire $l$ when bent becomes circumference of the loop, whose radius is given by $R = \dfrac{l}{2\pi} = \dfrac{314}{100\left(2 \times 3 . 14\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}m$

Magnetic moment of the coil is $M = IA$

$= 14 \times \pi{R}^{2}$

$= 14 \times \left(3 . 14\right) \times \dfrac{1}{4}$

$= 10 . 99 \approx 11 . 00A - {m}^{2}$

questions.q:
The current sensitivity of a galvanometer can be increased by :
(A) decreasing the number of turns
(B) increasing the magnetic field
(C) decreasing the area of the coil
(D) decreasing the torsional constant of the spring

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The current in the galvanometer is calculated by $i = \left(\dfrac{K}{NAB}\right)\theta$.

Therefore, the sensitivity of the galvanometer,

$\dfrac{d\theta}{di} = \dfrac{NAB}{K}$

Hence, only options B and D are correct.

questions.q:
As shown in the figure, a metallic rod of linear density $0 . 45kg{m}^{- 1}$ is lying horizontally on a smooth incline plane which makes an angle of $45 °$ with the horizontal. The minimum current flowing in the rod required to keep it stationary, when $0 . 15T$ magnetic field is acting on it in the vertical upward direction, will be

(Use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
For the wire to remain stationary, the net force acting on it should be zero.

Balancing the forces along the incline,

$mgsin45 ° = ILBcos45 °$

$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{m}{L}\right)\dfrac{g}{B}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\left(0 . 45\right)\left(10\right)}{0 . 15} = 30A$
questions.question:
As shown in the figure, a metallic rod of linear density $0 . 45kg{m}^{- 1}$ is lying horizontally on a smooth incline plane which makes an angle of $45 °$ with the horizontal. The minimum current flowing in the rod required to keep it stationary, when $0 . 15T$ magnetic field is acting on it in the vertical upward direction, will be

(Use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.explanation:
For the wire to remain stationary, the net force acting on it should be zero.

Balancing the forces along the incline,

$mgsin45 ° = ILBcos45 °$

$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{m}{L}\right)\dfrac{g}{B}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\left(0 . 45\right)\left(10\right)}{0 . 15} = 30A$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A cyclotron is used to accelerate protons. If the operating magnetic field is $1 . 0T$ and the radius of the cyclotron 'dees' is $60cm$, the kinetic energy of the accelerated protons in $MeV$ will be :
[use ${m}_{p} = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27}kg, e = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$]
questions.solution:
When the proton is rotated in a cyclotron its maximum velocity will be corresponding to the maximum radius of the circular path. We know that the radius of the circle in a magnetic field is given by,

$r = \dfrac{mv}{Bq} ⇒ v = \dfrac{Bqr}{m}$.

The kinetic energy will be,

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}{q}^{2}{r}^{2}}{2m} ⇒ K = \dfrac{{1}^{2} \times {\left(1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}\right)}^{2} \times {\left(0 . 6\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 13}}MeV ⇒ K = 18MeV$

questions.q: Two bar magnets oscillate in a horizontal plane in earth's magnetic field with time periods of $3s$ and $4s$respectively. If their moments of inertia are in the ratio of $3: 2$ then the ratio of their magnetic moments will be
questions.solution:
Torque on a bar magnet kept in a magnetic field is given by $τ = MBsin\theta$.

Hence, for small oscillations the time period of bar magnets is given by,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}} ⇒ M ∝ \dfrac{I}{{T}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{M}_{1}}{{M}_{2}} = \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} \times {\left(\dfrac{{T}_{2}}{{T}_{1}}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{M}_{1}}{{M}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2} \times {\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{8}{3}$

questions.q: Two concentric circular loops of radii ${r}_{1} = 30cm$ and ${r}_{2} = 50cm$ are placed in $X - Y$ plane as shown in the figure. A current $I = 7A$ is flowing through them in the direction as shown in figure. The net magnetic moment of this system of two circular loops is approximately
questions.solution:
Net magnetic moment of the system is

$\overset{\to}{M} = - I{A}_{1}\overset{^}{k} + I{A}_{2}\overset{^}{k}$ (Here currents in both circular loops are in opposite direction)

$\overset{\to}{M} = - I\pi{\left(0 . 5\right)}^{2}\overset{^}{k} + I\pi{\left(0 . 3\right)}^{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{M} = - 7 \times \dfrac{22}{7}\left(\dfrac{25}{100} - \dfrac{9}{100}\right)\overset{^}{k}$= - 22\left(\dfrac{16}{100}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{M} = - 3 . 52\overset{^}{k}A{m}^{2}$

$= - \dfrac{7}{2}\overset{^}{k}A{m}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A velocity selector consists of electric field $\overset{\to}{E} = E\overset{^}{k}$ and magnetic field $\overset{\to}{B} = B\overset{^}{j}$ with $B = 12mT$. The value $E$ required for an electron of energy $728eV$ moving along the positive $x$-axis to pass undeflected is

(Given, mass of electron $= 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$)
questions.solution:
Fiven that $\overset{\to}{E} = E\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{B} = 12\overset{^}{j}mT$

Kinetic energy$= 728eV$

Kinetic energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$⇒ 728eV = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times {v}^{2}$

$⇒ 728 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times {v}^{2}$

$⇒ v = 16 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}$

For electron to move undeflected net force on it should be zero.

$⇒ eE = evB$

$⇒ E = vB = 16 \times {10}^{6} \times 12 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ E = 192 \times {10}^{3}V{m}^{- 1} = 192kV{m}^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge particle is moving in a uniform magnetic field $\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)T$. If it has an acceleration of $\left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j}\right)m{s}^{- 2}$, then the value of $\alpha$ will be
questions.solution:
The magnetic force on a moving charged particle is given by $\overset{\to}{F} = q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$. Therefore, we know that the magnetic force is perpendicular to the magnetic field. Therefore, the resulting acceleration will also be perpendicular to the magnetic field. As the scalar product of two mutually perpendicular vectors is zero,

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{B} = 0 ⇒ \left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2\alpha - 12 = 0 ⇒ \alpha = 6$

questions.q: ${B}_{X}$ and ${B}_{Y}$ are the magnetic field at the centre of two coils of two coils $X$ and $Y$ respectively, each carrying equal current. If coil $X$ has $200$ turns and $20cm$ radius and coil $Y$ has $400$ turns and $20cm$ radius, the ratio of ${B}_{X}$ and ${B}_{Y}$ is
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of a single coil is $B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}$

If $N$ number of loops are kept closely $B = N\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}\right)$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{{B}_{x}}{{B}_{y}} = \dfrac{{N}_{x}}{{N}_{y}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{B}_{x}}{{B}_{y}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The electric current in a circular coil of $2$ turns produces a magnetic induction ${B}_{1}$ at its centre. The coil is unwound and is rewound into a circular coil of $5$ turns and the same current produces a magnetic induction ${B}_{2}$ at its centre.
The ratio of $\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}}$ is:
questions.solution:
Magnetic field on the centre of a circular current coil is given by $B = \dfrac{N{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}$, here, $N$ is number of turns, $i$ is current and $R$ is radius of loop.

Now, for, $N = 2$, magnetic field, ${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{N}_{1}{\mu}_{0}i}{2{R}_{1}}$

For ${N}_{2} = 5$

Radius of coil $= {R}_{2} = \dfrac{{N}_{1} \times {R}_{1}}{{N}_{2}}$

Magnetic field, ${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{N}_{2}{\mu}_{0}i}{2{R}_{2}}$

Thus, the ratio is $\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}} = \dfrac{{N}_{2}}{{N}_{1}}\dfrac{{R}_{1}}{{R}_{2}} = \dfrac{{N}_{2}}{{N}_{1}} \times \dfrac{{N}_{2}}{{N}_{1}}$

$\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}} = \dfrac{25}{4}$

questions.q: Two charged particles, having same kinetic energy, are allowed to pass through a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the direction of motion. If the ratio of radii of their circular paths is $6: 5$ and their respective masses ratio is $9: 4$. Then, the ratio of their charges will be
questions.solution:
Radius of charged particle moving in circular path $R = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$, here, $B$ is magnetic field and $K$ is kinetic energy.

So, $q = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{RB}$

Now, ratio of the charges is $\dfrac{{q}_{1}}{{q}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}}} \times \dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4}} \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

questions.q: Two long current carrying conductors are placed parallel to each other at a distance of $8cm$ between them. The magnitude of magnetic field produced at mid-point between the two conductors due to current flowing in them is $300\mu T$. The equal current flowing in the two conductors is :
questions.solution:
Magnetic field in parallel wires is given by $B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2\pid}$

At midway, $\text{distance} = \dfrac{d}{2}$

$∵ \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{\dfrac{2\pid}{2}} \times 2 = B$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{\pi} \times \dfrac{2I}{d} = B$

$⇒ \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 2I}{0 . 08} = 300 \times {10}^{- 6}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 0 . 08}{2 \times 4 \times {10}^{- 7}} = 30A$

As ${B}_{net} \ne 0$, so the wires are carrying current in opposite direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement $I$: The electric force changes the speed of the charged particle and hence changes its kinetic energy; whereas the magnetic force does not change the kinetic energy of the charged particle.
Statement $II$: The electric force accelerates the positively charged particle perpendicular to the direction of electric field. The magnetic force accelerates the moving charged particle along the direction of magnetic field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are correct.
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are incorrect.
Statement $I$ is correct but Statement $II$ is incorrect.
Statement $I$ is incorrect but Statement $II$ is correct.
questions.solution:
When a charged particle moves in an electric field, the field applies an electric force $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{E}\right)$ along the field, so work done by electric field is non-zero resulting in accelerated motion, thus kinetic energy changes.

When a particle moves in a uniform magnetic field, the force due to magnetic field on it is perpendicular to its velocity, as force $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$.
Since the magnetic field is constant, so force is constant. So, its direction of velocity constantly changes, but magnitude of velocity remains same. Hence, kinetic energy also does not change.

Electric field accelerates the particle in the direction of field $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{E} = m\overset{\to}{a}\right)$and magnetic field accelerates the particle perpendicular to the field $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B} = m\overset{\to}{a}\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge particle moves along circular path in a uniform magnetic field in a cyclotron. The kinetic energy of the charge particle increases to $4$ times its initial value. What will be the ratio of new radius to the original radius of circular path of the charge particle?
questions.solution:
Radius of a charged particle moving in a magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity is given by, $R = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$.

$mv$ can be written in terms of kinetic energy as $mv = \sqrt{2m\left(KE\right)}$. Therefore,

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2m\left(KE\right)}}{qB}$

$⇒ R ∝ \sqrt{KE} ⇒ \dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{1}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two parallel, long wires are kept $0 . 20m$ apart in vacuum, each carrying current of $xA$ in the same direction. If the force of attraction per meter of each wire is $2 \times {10}^{- 6}N$, then the value of $x$ is approximately
questions.solution:
Force per unit length between two parallel wires is $\dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{1}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$

Here, ${i}_{1} = {i}_{2} = i$ and $\dfrac{F}{l} = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}N$

Then, $2 \times {10}^{- 6} = \dfrac{4{\pi}^{2} \times {10}^{- 7}{i}^{2}}{2\pi \times 0 . 2}$

$⇒ {i}^{2} = \sqrt{2} ⇒ i = 1 . 4A$

Hence, $x = 1 . 4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An infinitely long hollow conducting cylinder with radius $R$ carries a uniform current along its surface.

Choose the correct representation of magnetic field $\left(B\right)$as a function of radial distance $\left(r\right)$ from the axis of cylinder.
questions.solution:
According to Ampere's law,

$∮ \overset{\to}{B} \cdot d \overset{\to}{l} = {\mu}_{0}i$

Inside the hollow cylinder, current will be zero. Therefore, magnetic field will also be zero.

Outside the cylinder,

$B2\pir = {\mu}_{0}i ⇒ B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\pir} ⇒ B ∝ \dfrac{1}{r}$

Hence, the correct answer is D.

questions.q: A singly ionized magnesium atom $\left(A = 24\right)$ ion is accelerated to kinetic energy $5keV$, and is projected perpendicularly into a magnetic field $B$ of the magnitude $0 . 5T$. The radius of path formed will be _____ $cm .$
questions.solution:
The radius of circle formed by a charged particle in a magnetic field perpendicular to the velocity is given by,

$R = \dfrac{mV}{qB} ⇒ R = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 \times 24 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27} \times 5000 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 0 . 5} = 979 \times {10}^{- 4}m ≃ 10cm$

Two long parallel conductors ${S}_{1}$ and ${S}_{2}$ are separated by a distance $10cm$ and carrying currents of $4A$ and $2A$ respectively. The conductors are placed along $x$-axis in $X - Y$ plane. There is a point $P$ located between the conductors (as shown in figure).
A charge particle of $3\pi$ coulomb is passing through the point $P$ with velocity $\overset{\to}{v} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)m{s}^{- 1}$; where $\overset{^}{i}$ & $\overset{^}{j}$ represents unit vector along $x$ & $y$axis respectively.
The force acting on the charge particle is $4\pi \times {10}^{- 5}\left(- x\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j}\right)N$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Net magnetic field at $P$ is ${B}_{Net} = \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0} \times {i}_{1}}{2\pi{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{2}}{2\pi{r}_{2}}\right)\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

${B}_{Net} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}4}{2\pi \times \dfrac{4}{100}} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}2}{2\pi \times \dfrac{6}{100}}$

$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{\pi} \times 100\left[\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{6}\right]$

$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{\pi} \times 100\left[\dfrac{4}{2 \times 6}\right]$

$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0} \times 100}{3\pi}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, force acting on charge particle is$\overset{\to}{F} = q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right) = 3\pi\left[2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right]\dfrac{{\mu}_{0} \times 100}{3\pi}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\left[2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right] \times 100\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 4\pi \times {10}^{- 5}\left[2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{i}\right]$

$∴ x = 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A deuteron and a proton moving with equal kinetic energy enter into to a uniform magnetic field at right angle to the field. If ${r}_{d}$ and ${r}_{p}$ are the radii of their circular paths respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{{r}_{d}}{{r}_{p}}$ will be $\sqrt{x}: 1$ where $x$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
As we know, radius of circular path followed by charged particle under perpendicular magnetic field is given by,

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$ and $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Therefore,

$⇒ R = \dfrac{\sqrt{2m\left(KE\right)}}{qB}$ Then, $R ∝ \dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{q}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{R}_{d}}{{R}_{p}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{d}}{{m}_{p}}} \times \dfrac{{q}_{p}}{{q}_{d}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{1}} \times \dfrac{1}{1} = \sqrt{2}: 1$

Thus, $x = 2$.

Thus, $x = 2$.

questions.q: A bar magnet having a magnetic moment of $2 . 0 \times {10}^{5}J{T}^{- 1}$, is placed along the direction of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $B = 14 \times {10}^{- 5}T$. The work done in rotating the magnet slowly through $60 °$ from the direction of field is
questions.solution:
Work done by the external force is equal to the change in the potential energy,

${W}_{ext} = \DeltaU = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = - MBcos{\theta}_{2} + MBcos{\theta}_{1}$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = MB\left(cos{\theta}_{1} - cos{\theta}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = 14 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 2 \times {10}^{5}\left(cos0 ° - cos60 °\right)$

$⇒ {W}_{ext} = 14 \times 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 14J$

questions.q: A metal surface is illuminated by a radiation of wavelength $4500\overset{∘}{A}$. The ejected photo-electron enters a constant magnetic field of $2mT$ making an angle of $90 °$ with the magnetic field. If it starts revolving in a circular path of radius $2mm$, the work function of the metal is approximately
questions.solution:
From the Einstein's photoelectric equation $K = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - ϕ ⇒ ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - K$

Now $R = \dfrac{mv}{Bq} ⇒ v = \dfrac{RBq}{m} ⇒ K = \dfrac{{R}^{2}{B}^{2}{q}^{2}}{2m}$

Therefore, $ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{{R}^{2}{B}^{2}{q}^{2}}{2m} = \dfrac{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4500 \times {10}^{- 10}} - \dfrac{{\left(2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}} ⇒ ϕ = \left(4 . 42 - 2 . 25\right) \times {10}^{- 19}J = \dfrac{2 . 27}{1 . 6}eV = 1 . 36eV$

questions.q: Two $10cm$ long, straight wires, each carrying a current of $5A$ are kept parallel to each other. If each wire experienced a force of ${10}^{- 5}N$, then separation between the wires is _____ $cm .$
questions.solution:
Given: $F = {10}^{- 5}N$

Force between wires $\dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{1}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$, where, $d$ is separation between them.

$⇒ \dfrac{{10}^{- 5}}{0 . 1} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 25}{d}$

$⇒ d = 50 \times {10}^{- 3}m = 5cm$

questions.q:
Given below two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Non-polar materials do not have any permanent dipole moment.

Reason (R): When a non-polar material is placed in an electric field, the centre of the positive charge distribution of it's individual atom or molecule coincides with the centre of the negative charge distribution.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Non-polar materials do not have any permanent dipole moment. This statement is true.

When a non-polar material is placed in an electric field, centre of positive charge is pushed in the direction of the electric field and centre of the negative charge is pushed in the direction opposite to the electric field. Hence, they don't coincide. Therefore, reason is false.

questions.q: A long solenoid carrying a current produces a magnetic field $B$ along its axis. If the current is doubled and the number of turns per $cm$ is halved, the new value of magnetic field will be equal to
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to long solenoid along its axis is given as,

$B = {\mu}_{0}nI$, where $n$ is the number of turns in the solenoid per unit length, $I$ is current in the solenoid and ${\mu}_{0}$ is a constant called the permeability of free space.

$⇒ \dfrac{{B}_{1}}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{I}_{1}}{{n}_{2}{I}_{2}}$

According to the question, ${n}_{2} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}}{2}\text{and}{I}_{2} = 2{I}_{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{B}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}}{\left(\dfrac{{n}_{1}}{2}\right)} \times \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{2{I}_{1}} ⇒ {B}_{2} = B$; means, the magnetic field remains the same.
