questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long straight wire with a circular cross-section having radius $R$, is carrying a steady current $I$. The current $I$ is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. Then the variation of magnetic field due to current $I$ with distance $r\left(r < R\right)$ from its centre will be
questions.solution:
Using Ampere's law and noting that the steady current is uniformly distributed over the cross-section of the cylindrical wire.

$B = \left[\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}Ir}{2\pi{R}^{2}}, r \le R \\ \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2\pir}, r > R\end{array}\right]$

Thus, magnetic field $B ∝ r$ from the centre for $r < R$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : In an uniform magnetic field, speed and energy remains the same for a moving charged particle.

Reason (R): Moving charged particle experiences magnetic force perpendicular to its direction of motion.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The force experienced by the charge particle is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity at all instants as $\overset{\to}{F} = q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$.

Hence, the magnetic force cannot bring any change in the speed of the charged particle. Since, the speed remains constant, the kinetic energy also remains constant.

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius $r$, due to current I flowing through it, is $B$. The magnetic field at a point along the axis at a distance $\dfrac{r}{2}$ from the centre is :
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the circle is, $B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}$

Magnetic field at the point on the axis is,

${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i{R}^{2}}{2{\left({R}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}} ⇒ {B}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i{R}^{2}}{2{\left({R}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)}^{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}} ⇒ {B}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2{\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}R} = {\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)}^{3}B$

questions.q:
The temperature of $3 . 00mol$ of an ideal diatomic gas is increased by $40 . 0 ° C$ without changing the pressure of the gas. The molecules in the gas rotate but do not oscillate. If the ratio of change in internal energy of the gas to the amount of workdone by the gas is $\dfrac{x}{10} .$ Then the value of $x$ (round off to the nearest integer) is $_________ .

$($ Given $\leftR = 8 . 31J{mol}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}\right)$

$
questions.solution:
First, recall the formula of change in internal energy in terms of molar specific heat at constant volume and change in temperature, $∆ U = n{C}_{V}\DeltaT$, for diatomic gas, ${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2}R = \dfrac{5}{2}R$, $⇒ ∆ U = n \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times R\DeltaT$

$⇒ \dfrac{\DeltaU}{W} = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{2}nR\DeltaT}{nR\DeltaT} = \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{25}{10}$

So, $x = 25$

$\overset{\to}{M} = \dfrac{magnetic moment \left(\overset{\to}{m}\right)}{V}$

questions.q: The fractional change in the magnetic field intensity at a distance $r$ from centre on the axis of current carrying coil of radius $a$ to the magnetic field intensity at the centre of the same coil is: (Take $r < a$)
questions.solution:
As we know,

${B}_{axis} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{iR}^{2}}{2{\left({R}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}\text{where}, R = a$

${B}_{\text{centre}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2a}$

$∴ {B}_{\text{axis}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{ia}^{2}}{2{\left({a}^{2} + {r}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}$

$∴$ fractional change in magnetic field $= \dfrac{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2a} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i{a}^{2}}{2{\left({a}^{2} + {r}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}}{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2a}} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right)\right]}^{3 / 2}}$

$\approx 1 - \left[1 - \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right] = \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}$

$∴$ fractional change in magnetic field $= \dfrac{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2a} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i{a}^{2}}{2{\left({a}^{2} + {r}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}}{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2a}} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right)\right]}^{3 / 2}}$

$\approx 1 - \left[1 - \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right] = \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}$

questions.q: A proton, a deuteron and an $\alpha$ particle are moving with same momentum in a uniform magnetic field. The ratio of magnetic forces acting on them ______ is and their speed is ______ in the ratio.
questions.solution:
$F = q\left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right) = \dfrac{q}{m} \left(\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)

$⇒ F ∝ $\dfrac{q}{m}

thus,
${F}_{1}: {F}_{2}: {F}_{3} = $\dfrac{q1}{{m}_{1}}$: $\dfrac{q2}{{m}_{2}}$: $\dfrac{q3}{{m}_{3}}= \dfrac{e}{mp}$: $\dfrac{e}{2{m}_{p}}$: $\dfrac{2e}{4{m}_{p}}= \dfrac{1}{1}$: $\dfrac{1}{2}$: $\dfrac{2}{4}=2: 1: 1$

Now for speed calculation, $P = constant ⇒ v ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}

thus ${v}_{1}: {v}_{2}: {v}_{3} = $\dfrac{1}{{m}_{p}}$: $\dfrac{1}{2{m}_{p}}$: $\dfrac{1}{4{m}_{p}}= \dfrac{1}{1}$: $\dfrac{1}{2}$: $\dfrac{1}{4}=4: 2: 1$.

$⇒ F ∝ \dfrac{q}{m}$

thus,
${F}_{1}: {F}_{2}: {F}_{3} = \dfrac{{q}_{1}}{{m}_{1}}: \dfrac{{q}_{2}}{{m}_{2}}: \dfrac{{q}_{3}}{{m}_{3}}$= \dfrac{e}{{m}_{p}}: \dfrac{e}{2{m}_{p}}: \dfrac{2e}{4{m}_{p}}$= \dfrac{1}{1}: \dfrac{1}{2}: \dfrac{2}{4}$= 2: 1: 1$

Now for speed calculation, $P = constant ⇒ v ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$

thus ${v}_{1}: {v}_{2}: {v}_{3} = \dfrac{1}{{m}_{p}}: \dfrac{1}{2{m}_{p}}: \dfrac{1}{4{m}_{p}}$= \dfrac{1}{1}: \dfrac{1}{2}: \dfrac{1}{4}$= 4: 2: 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Magnetic fields at two points on the axis of a circular coil at a distance of $0 . 05m$ and $0 . 2m$ from the centre are in the ratio $8: 1$. The radius of coil is _______ .
questions.solution:
We know, the magnetic field on the axis of a current carrying circular ring is given by

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{2NIA}{{\left({R}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{B}_{1}}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{8}{1} = {\left[\dfrac{{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2}}{{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}}\right]}^{3 / 2}$

$4\left[{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}\right] = \left[{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2}\right]$

$4{R}^{2} - {R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} - 4 \times {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}$

$4{R}^{2} - {R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} - {\left(0 . 1\right)}^{2}$

$3{R}^{2} = 0 . 3 \times 0 . 1$

${R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 1\right)}^{2} ⇒ R = 0 . 1$
questions.question: Magnetic fields at two points on the axis of a circular coil at a distance of $0 . 05m$ and $0 . 2m$ from the centre are in the ratio $8: 1$. The radius of coil is _______ .
questions.explanation:
We know, the magnetic field on the axis of a current carrying circular ring is given by

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{2NIA}{{\left({R}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{B}_{1}}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{8}{1} = {\left[\dfrac{{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2}}{{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}}\right]}^{3 / 2}$

$4\left[{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}\right] = \left[{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2}\right]$

$4{R}^{2} - {R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} - 4 \times {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}$

$4{R}^{2} - {R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} - {\left(0 . 1\right)}^{2}$

$3{R}^{2} = 0 . 3 \times 0 . 1$

${R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 1\right)}^{2} ⇒ R = 0 . 1$

questions.q: An iron rod of volume ${10}^{- 3}{m}^{3}$ and relative permeability $1000$ is placed as core in a solenoid with$10turns{cm}^{- 1}$ . If a current of $0 . 5A$ is passed through the solenoid, then the magnetic moment of the rod will be :
questions.solution:
Given,

Volume of iron rod is, $V = {10}^{- 3}{m}^{3}$

Relative permeability, ${\mu}_{r} = 1000$

No of turns per unit length of solenoid is, $n = \dfrac{N}{l} = 10turns{cm}^{- 1} = 1000turns{m}^{- 1}$

Current through the solenoid is, $i = 0 . 5A$

Magnetic moment of an iron core solenoid is given by,

$M = ( {\mu}_{r} - 1 ) NiA$

$⇒ M = \left({\mu}_{r} - 1\right)Ni\dfrac{V}{l} = \left({\mu}_{r} - 1\right)\dfrac{N}{l}iV$

$⇒ M = \left(1000 - 1\right) \times 1000 \times 0 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ M = 499 . 5 \approx 500A{m}^{2}$

The coil is kept initially in a vertical position and it can rotate freely around a horizontal diameter. When a uniform magnetic field of $4T$ is applied along the vertical, it starts rotating around its horizontal diameter. The angular speed the coil acquires after rotating by ${60}^{o}$ will be :
questions.solution:
From energy conservation

$\dfrac{1}{2}{I \omega}^{2} = {U}_{n} - {U}_{t}$

$= - MBcos60 ° - ( - MB )$

$\dfrac{MB}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I \omega}^{2}$

$\dfrac{20 \times 4}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ( 08 ) {m}^{2}$

$100 = {\omega}^{2}$

$\omega = 10rad$

questions.q: A wire $A$, bent in the shape of an arc of a circle, carrying a current of $2A$ and having radius $2$ cm and another wire $B$, also bent in the shape of an arc of a circle, carrying a current of $3A$ and having radius of $4\text{cm}$, are placed as shown in the figure. The ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wires $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ at the common centre $\text{O}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given,

Current in the arc $A$ is ${i}_{1} = 2A$

Current in the arc $B$ is ${i}_{2} = 3A$

Radius of arc $A$ is ${R}_{1} = 2cm$

Radius of arc $B$ is ${R}_{2} = 4cm$

Magnetic field at the centre of circular current carrying arc is given by

${B}_{C} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left(\theta\right) . . . ( 1 )$

Where, $\theta$ is the angle subtended at centre.

Magnetic field at the centre due to arc $A$ and $B$ is given by

${B}_{A} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{1}}{4{\pi R}_{1}}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

${B}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{i}_{2}}{4{\pi R}_{2}}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) . . . \left(3\right)$

Dividing equation (2) by (1), we get

$⇒ \dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{{i}_{1}}{{i}_{2}} \times \dfrac{{R}_{2}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{{R}_{1}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{4}{2} \times \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{5\pi}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{6}{5}$

questions.q:
A small bar magnet is moved through a coil at constant speed from one end to the other. Which of the following series of observations will be seen on the galvanometer $\text{G}$ attached across the coil?

&

Three positions shown describe: (a) the magnet's entry (b) magnet is completely inside and (c) magnet's exit.
questions.solution:
(a) When the bar magnet entering the coil the magnetic flux link with the coil increases, and according to the Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the emf will induce in the coil, which in tern induces current and galvanometer shows the deflection towards right.

(b) When the bar magnet is inside the coil no change in magnetic flux link with the coil, therefore galvanometer do not show deflection.

(c) When the bar magnet exit from the coil the magnetic flux link with the coil decreases, and according to the Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the emf will induce in the coil, in opposite direction which in tern induces current and galvanometer shows the deflection towards left.

questions.q: Magnitude of magnetic field (in SI units) at the centre of a hexagonal shape coil of side $10cm, 50$ turns and carrying current$I$  (Ampere) in units of $\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{\pi}$ is :
questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the current-carrying finite length wire is given by

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\piR}\left[sin{\theta}_{1} + sin{\theta}_{2}\right]$

Here for hexagonal shape coil, ${\theta}_{1} = {\theta}_{2} = 30 °$.

So, the net magnetic field at the centre will be $B = 50 \times 6 \times \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\pi\left(\dfrac{10}{100}cos30 °\right)}\left[sin30 ° + sin30 °\right]$

$B = 2 \times 75 \times 10\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{\sqrt{3}\pi}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$B = \dfrac{1500}{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{\pi} = \left(500\sqrt{3}\right)\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{\pi}$

questions.q: A charged particle (mass $m$ and charge $q$) moves along $X$ axis with velocity ${V}_{0}$. When it passes through the origin it enters a region having uniform electric field $\overset{\to}{E} = - E\overset{^}{j}$ which extends upto $x = d$. Equation of path of electron in the region $x > d$ is:
questions.solution:
$x > d$path is straight line

$\dfrac{- y - \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}}{x - d} = \dfrac{at}{{V}_{0}}$

$\dfrac{- y - \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}}{at} = \dfrac{x - d}{{V}_{0}}$

$\dfrac{- y}{at} - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d}{{V}_{0}} = \dfrac{x}{{V}_{0}} - \dfrac{d}{{V}_{0}}$

$\dfrac{- my{V}_{0}}{qEd} = \dfrac{x}{{V}_{0}} - \dfrac{d}{2{V}_{0}}$

$y = \dfrac{- qEd}{m{V}_{0}}\left(\dfrac{x}{{V}_{0}} - \dfrac{d}{2{V}_{0}}\right)$

$y = \dfrac{qEd}{m{V}_{0}^{2}}\left(\dfrac{d}{2} - x\right)$.

questions.q: An electron gun is placed inside a long solenoid of radius $R$ on its axis. The solenoid has $n$ turns/length and carries a current $I .$ The electron gun shoots an electron along the radius of the solenoid with speed $v .$ If the electron does not hit the surface of the solenoid, maximum possible value of $v$ is (all symbols have their standard meaning):
questions.solution:
Magnetic Field Inside Solenoid is $B = {\mu}_{0}nI$

Velocity $ν$ has given to the electron

So, Magnetic Force

$F = qνB$

as $ν$and $B$ are perpendicular.

In a magnetic field, charge will move on a circular path. Here, If radius is just less than or equal to radius of solenoid then the electron does not hit the surface.

$F = qνB = \dfrac{m{ν}^{2}}{R} ⇒ mν = qBRasq = eν = \dfrac{eBR}{m}So, V = \dfrac{e{\mu}_{0}nIR}{m}$

If the radius of the largest circular path followed by the electrons is $10mm$ , the work function of the metal is close to:

$K{E}_{max} = E - ϕ$

questions.q: A long, straight Wire of radius a carries a current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. The ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wire at distance $\dfrac{a}{3}$ and $2a$ , respectively from the axis of the wire is:

$\dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q:
A charged particle of mass ‘ $m$ ’ and charge ‘ $q$ ’ moving under the influence of uniform electric field $\overset{\to}{\text{E}}\overset{^}{i}$ and a uniform magnetic field $\overset{\to}{\text{B}}\overset{^}{k}$ follows a trajectory from point P to Q as shown in figure. The velocities at P and Q are respectively, $v\overset{\to}{i} and - 2v\overset{\to}{j}$ . Then which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) are the correct? (Trajectory shown is schematic and not to scale)



$\left(A\right) E = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{qa}\right)
\left(B\right) Rate of work done by the electric field at P is \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{m{v}^{3}}{a}\right)$
$\left(C\right)$ Rate of work done by both the fields at Q is zero
$\left(D\right)$ The difference between the magnitude of angular momentum of the particle at P and Q is $2mav$ .
questions.solution:
$( A )$ by work energy theorem

${W}_{mag} + {W}_{ele} = \dfrac{1}{2}m ( 2v{)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}m ( v{)}^{2}$

$0 + {qE}_{0}2a = \dfrac{3}{2}{mv}^{2}$
${E}_{0} = \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac{{mv}^{2}}{qa}$

$( B )$ Rate of work done at $A =$ power of electric force

$= {qE}_{0}V$
$= \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac{{mv}^{3}}{a}$

$( C )$ at $Q, \dfrac{dw}{dt} = 0$ for both forces

$\left(D\right) \Delta\overset{\to}{L} = ( - m2\text{v}2a\overset{^}{k} ) - ( - \text{mvak} )$

$| \Delta\overset{\to}{L} | = 3mva$

questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{{B}_{0}} = {\left(\overset{\to}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{1} + {\left(\overset{\to}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{2} + {\left(\overset{\to}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{3} + {\left(\overset{\to}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{4}$
$\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[sin ⁡ 90 ° - sin45 °\right]⨂ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}⨀ +$\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR} ( sin45 ° + sin90 ° ) ⨀$
$- \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right] + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 1\right]⨀$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[- 1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 2\pi + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 1\right]⨀ = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[\sqrt{2} + 2\pi\right]⨀ = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\piR}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \pi\right]⨀$

questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by $\overset{\to}{E} = {E}_{0}\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}cos ⁡ \left(kz + \omegat\right)$ . At $t = 0$ , a positively charged particle is at the point $\left(x, y, z\right) = \left(0, 0, \dfrac{\pi}{k}\right)$ . If its instantaneous velocity at $\left(t = 0\right)$ is ${v}_{0}\overset{^}{k}$ , the force acting on it due to the wave is:
questions.solution:
Force due to electric field is in direction $– \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{2}}{E}_{0}$
Force due to magnetic filed is in direction $q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{v} | | \overset{^}{k}$
$∴$ it is parallel to $\overset{\to}{E}$
$∴$ net force is antiparallel to $\dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{2}}$ .

A ring of radius $2R$ is placed coaxially near its middle. During the time interval $0 \le t \le 1,$ the induced current $\left({I}_{R}\right)$ and the induced $EMF \left({V}_{R}\right) in the ring change as:$
options: Direction of ${I}_{R}$ remains unchanged and ${V}_{R}$ is maximum at $t = 0.5$
At $t = 0.25$ direction of ${I}_{R}$ reverses and ${V}_{R}$ is maximum
Direction of ${I}_{R}$ remains unchanged and ${V}_{R}$ is zero at $t = 0.25$
At $t = 0.5$ direction of ${I}_{R}$ reverses and ${V}_{R}$ is zero
questions.solution:
$I = {I}_{0}t - {I}_{0}{t}^{2}$
$ϕ = BA$
$ϕ = {\mu}_{0}nIA$
${V}_{R} = - \dfrac{dϕ}{dt} = - {\mu}_{0}nA{I}_{0}\left(1 - 2t\right)$
${V}_{R} = 0$ at $t = \dfrac{1}{2}$
And ${I}_{R} = \dfrac{{V}_{R}}{Resistanceofloop} = 0$

questions.q: A square loop is carrying a steady current $I$ and the magnitude of its magnetic dipole moment is $m$ . If this square loop is changed to a circular loop and it carries the same current, the magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment of circular loop will be:
questions.solution:
Let the side of square loop be $a$.
The magnetic dipole is$∴ m = I{a}^{2}$
$a = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}$
Radius of circular loop $r$ related to $a$ as circumference of circular loop is equal to perimeter of square loop.
$2\pir = 4a = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}$
$r = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}$
$∴$ New dipole moment ${m}^{'} = \pi{\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}\right)}^{2}I$
$= \dfrac{4m}{\pi}$

questions.q:
The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of an equilateral triangular loop of side $1m$ which is carrying a current of $10A$ is:

[Take ${\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}N{A}^{- 2}$ ]
questions.solution:
The perpendicular distance of centroid from any side, $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}m$
Magnetic field due to one side.
${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{µ}_{o}I}{4\pir} [ cos{\theta}_{1} + cos{\theta}_{2} ]$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0} ( 10 )}{4\pir\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\right)}\left[cos{30}^{°} + cos{30}^{°}\right]$
$= \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{\pi}{\mu}_{0}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right] = \dfrac{15{\mu}_{0}}{\pi}$
Net magnetic field $B = 3{B}_{1} = \dfrac{45}{\pi}{\mu}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{\pi} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}$
$= 180 \times {10}^{- 7}T$
$= 18\muT$

questions.q: Two wires $A$ & $B$ are carrying currents ${I}_{1}$ and ${I}_{2}$ as shown in the figure. The separation between them is $d$ . A third wire $C$ carrying a current $I$ is to be kept parallel to them at a distance $x$ from $A$ such that the net force acting on it is zero. The possible values of $x$ are:
questions.solution:
As current in $A and B$ are opposite in direction, net force on $C$ can never be zero if it is kept between
$A and B$ .

$∴ \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}I}{2\pix} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I{I}_{2}}{2\pi\left(x \pm d\right)}$
${I}_{1}\left(x \pm d\right) = {I}_{2}x$
$\left({I}_{2} - {I}_{1}\right)x = \pm {I}_{1}d$
$x = \pm \dfrac{{I}_{1}d}{{I}_{2} - {I}_{1}}$

questions.q: A rigid square loop of side $‘a’$ and carrying current ${I}_{2}$ is lying on a horizontal surface near a long current ${I}_{1}$ carrying wire in the same plane as shown in figure. The net force on the loop due to the wire will be:
questions.solution:
Force on segment 1-2 and 3-4 will get cancel out.
Force on segment 4-1,
${F}_{1} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pia} \times a$ toward Right
Force on segment 2-3:
${F}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pi ( 2a )} \times a$ toward left
Net force on loop:
${F}_{net} = {F}_{1} - {F}_{2}$ toward Right
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pi} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{4\pi}$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{4\pi}$ toward Right or repulsive

questions.q: A rectangular coil (Dimension $5cm \times 2.5cm$ ) with $100$ turns, carrying a current of $3A$ in the clock-wise direction, is kept centered at the origin and in the $X - Z$ plane. A magnetic field of $1T$ is applied along $X - axis$ . If the coil is tilted through $45 °$ about $Z - axis$ , then the torque on the coil is:

$= 100 \times 3 \times \left(5 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 2.5 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) \times 1 \times sin{45}^{o}$
$= 0.27Nm$

questions.q: Two magnetic dipoles $X$ and $Y$ are placed at a separation $d$ , with their axes perpendicular to each other. The dipole moment of $Y$ is twice that of $X$ . A particle of charge $q$ is passing through their mid-point $P$ , at angle $\theta = {45}^{o}$ with the horizontal line, as shown in figure. What would be the magnitude of force on the particle at that instant? ( $d$ is much larger than the dimension of the dipole)
questions.solution:
${B}_{X} = 2\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\right)\dfrac{M}{d / 2}$ along $x$ -axis
${B}_{\text{Y}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{\left(2M\right)}{\left(d / 2\right)}$ along $y$ -axis
${B}_{\text{X}} = {B}_{Y}$

Hence ${B}_{net}$ will be at ${45}^{o}$ from $x$ -axis.
Now, velocity and magnetic field are in same direction. Hence no force will act on the particle.

questions.q: A proton and an $\alpha$- particle (with their masses in the ratio of $1: 4$ and charges in the ratio of $1: 2$ ) are accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V .$ If a uniform magnetic field $\left(B\right)$ is set up perpendicular to their velocities, the ratio of the radii ${r}_{p}: {r}_{\alpha}$ of the circular paths described by them will be:
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a charge $q$ of mass $m$ in potential is given by,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = qV$

$mv = \sqrt{2mqV}$

Then, the radius of the charge will be,

$r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB}$

$⇒ r ∝ \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{q}}$

Hence, the ratio of radius of proton to $\alpha$-particle,

$\dfrac{{r}_{p}}{{r}_{\alpha}} =$\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{2}{1}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

$\omega = 2\pinrad{s}^{- 1}$



$dQ = ρdx$

Current due to elementary charge $dQ$

Magnetic dipole moment

$∫ dM = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{l}\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} \times \dfrac{{ρ}_{0}}{l} \times xdx\pi{x}^{2}$

$M = \dfrac{{\pinρ}_{0}{l}^{3}}{4}$

questions.q: In a certain region static electric and magnetic fields exist. The magnetic field is given by $\overset{\to}{B} = {B}_{0}\left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)$. ${F}_{e} = - {q}_{0}{v}_{0}{B}_{0}\left(\overset{\to}{V} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$

${F}_{e} = - {q}_{0}{v}_{0}{B}_{0}\left[\left(3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)\right]$

${\overset{\to}{F}}_{e} = - q{v}_{0}{B}_{0} ( 14\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k} )$

The electric field produced by the test charge is $∵ \overset{\to}{E} = \dfrac{{\overset{\to}{f}}_{e}}{q} = - {v}_{0}{B}_{0} ( 14\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k} )$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A conducting metal circular-wire-loop of radius $r$ is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field which varies with time as $B = {B}_{0}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}},$ where ${B}_{0}andτ$ are constants at time $t = 0$. If the resistance of the loop is $R$, then the heat generated in the loop after a long time $\left(t \to \infty\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Here, $B = {B}_{0}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}$
Area of the circular loop, $A = \pi{r}^{2}$
Flux linked with the loop at any time $t$ ,
$ϕ = BA = \pi{r}^{2}{B}_{0}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}$
Emf induced in the loop, $ε = - \dfrac{dϕ}{dt} = \pi{r}^{2}{B}_{0}\dfrac{1}{τ}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}$
Net heat generated in the loop
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{{ε}^{2}}{R}dt = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}{r}^{4}{B}_{0}^{2}}{{τ}^{2}R}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}{e}^{- \dfrac{2t}{τ}}dt$
$= \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}{r}^{4}{B}_{0}^{2}}{{τ}^{2}R} \times \dfrac{1}{\left(- \dfrac{2}{τ}\right)} \times {\left[{e}^{- \dfrac{2t}{τ}}\right]}_{0}^{\infty}$
$= \dfrac{- {\pi}^{2}{r}^{4}{B}_{0}^{2}}{2{τ}^{2}R} \times τ\left(0 - 1\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}{r}^{4}{B}_{0}^{2}}{2τR}$

questions.q: Two identical wires $A$ and $B$, each of length $l$, carry the same current $I$ . Wire $A$ is bent into a circle of radius $R$ and wire $B$ is bent to form a square of side $a$. If ${B}_{A}$ and ${B}_{B}$ are the values of magnetic field at the centres of the circle and square respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}}$ is
questions.solution:
As length of both the wires is same, $2\piR = 4a$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{R} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{R} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

${B}_{A} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}$ and

${B}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{\pia}\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)$

Therefore, ratio will be $\dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R} \times \dfrac{\pia}{2\sqrt{2}{\mu}_{0}i}$

If ${B}_{A}$ and ${B}_{B}$ are the values of magnetic field at the centres of the circle and square respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}}$ is
questions.explanation:
As length of both the wires is same, $2\piR = 4a$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{R} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{R} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

${B}_{A} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}$ and

${B}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{\pia}\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)$

Therefore, ratio will be $\dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R} \times \dfrac{\pia}{2\sqrt{2}{\mu}_{0}i}$

$= \dfrac{\pia}{4\sqrt{2}R} = \dfrac{\pi}{4\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{8\sqrt{2}}$

A rectangular loop of sides $10cm$ and $5cm$, carrying a current $I$ of $12A$, is placed in different orientations as shown in the figure below.
(a) (b)

(c) (d)

If there is a uniform magnetic field of $0 . 3T$ in the positive $z$ direction, in which orientations the loop would be in $( i )$ stable equilibrium and $( ii )$ unstable equilibrium?
questions.solution:
For a magnetic dipole placed in a uniform magnetic field, the torque is given by $\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{M} \times \overset{\to}{B}$, and potential energy $U$ is given as,

$U = - \overset{\to}{M} \cdot \overset{\to}{B} = - MBcos\theta$

When $\overset{\to}{M}$ is in the same direction as $\overset{\to}{B}$ then $\overset{\to}{τ} = 0$ and $U$ is minimum = $- MB$ as $\theta = {0}^{o}$.$⇒$ Stable equilibrium is (b).

When $\overset{\to}{M}$ the opposite direction of $\overset{\to}{B}$, then $\overset{\to}{τ} = 0$ and $U$ is max = $+ MB$
As, $\theta = {180}^{o}$⇒$Unstable equilibrium in (d)

questions.q: Two coaxial solenoids of different radii carry current $I$ in the same direction. Let $\overset{\to}{{F}_{1}}$ be the magnetic force on the inner solenoid due to the outer one and $\overset{\to}{{F}_{2}}$ be the magnetic force on the outer solenoid due to the inner one. Then:
options: $\overset{\to}{{F}_{1}}$  is radially inwards and  $\overset{\to}{{F}_{2}}$  is radially outwards
questions.solution:
${S}_{2}$ is a solenoid with more radius than ${S}_{1}$, the magnetic field of the solenoid ${S}_{2}$ will be along the axis and constant, so the magnetic force on an element of solenoid ${S}_{1}$ will be,

$d \overset{\to}{F}1 = i\left(\overset{\to}{l} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$

$d \overset{\to}{F}1 = ilB\left(\overset{^}{j} \times \left(- \overset{^}{i}\right)\right) = iBl\overset{^}{k}$

Similarly, for just next coil the magnetic field is in same direction, but the current element is in opposite direction, so,

$d \overset{\to}{F}1 = ilB\left(- \overset{^}{j} \times \left(- \overset{^}{i}\right)\right) = - iBl\overset{^}{k}$.

From Symmetry, we can say that the overall force will be cancelled to the whole coil, hence, $\overset{\to}{F}1 = 0$

Similarly, from coil ${S}_{1}$ to ${S}_{2}$, The magnetic field of the inner solenoid is symmetric about its axis, but not exactly along the axis of the outer solenoid. As the outer solenoid is placed symmetrically the push of any coil will be equal and opposite to the pull of coil placed exactly the opposite distance from the centre. Hence, the net force on the outer coil will be zero, i.e., $\overset{\to}{F}2 = 0$.

For loop $B=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{nI}}{2 \mathrm{a}}$ where, $a$ is the radius of loop.

\mathrm{B}_{1}$:  $\mathrm{B}_{2}=1: 3
\end{aligned}
$

questions.q: A conductor lies along the z-axis at $- \text{1.5} \le \text{z} < \text{1.5} m$ and carries a fixed current of 10.0 A in ${- \overset{^}{\text{a}}}_{\text{z}}$ direction (see figure). For a field $\overset{\to}{\text{B}} = \text{3.0} \times 1 {0}^{- 4} {\text{e}}^{- \text{0.2x}} {\overset{^}{\text{a}}}_{\text{y}}$ T, find the power required to move the conductor at constant speed to x = 2.0 m, y = 0 m in $5 \times 1 {0}^{- 3} \text{s}$. Assume parallel motion along the x-axis.
questions.solution:
$\text{Power P} = \dfrac{\text{W}}{\text{\Delta} \text{t}}$

Force on conductor
$\overset{\to}{F} = I ( \overset{\to}{l} \times \overset{\to}{b} )$

$\overset{\to}{F} = -10( 3\overset{^}{a} z ) \times ( 3 \times {10}^{- 4} {e}^{- 0.2x} \overset{^}{a} y )$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{F} = 90 \times {10}^{- 4} ( {e}^{- 0.2x} )$ along with x-axis

work done on the conductor in moving along x-axis.

$W = \mathop{∫}_{x = 0}^{2}\overset{\to}{F} . \overset{\to}{dx}$

$\text{W} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2} \text{Bi} ℓ \text{dx} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2} 3 \times {\text{10}}^{- 4} {\text{e}}^{- \text{0.2x}} \times 3 \times \text{10dx}$= 90 \times {10}^{- 4}{\left[\dfrac{{e}^{- 0.2x}}{- 0.2}\right]}_{0}^{2}$

$= \text{450} \times {\text{10}}^{- 4} [ 1 - {\text{e}}^{- \text{0.4}} ] = \text{180} \times {\text{10}}^{- 4} ( \text{Using} {\text{e}}^{- \text{x}} = 1 - \text{x} )$

$\text{P} = \dfrac{\text{W}}{\text{\Delta} \text{t}} = \dfrac{\text{180} \times {\text{10}}^{- 4}}{5 \times {\text{10}}^{- 3}} = \text{3.6 W.}$

Hence, closest option is 2.97 W.
(if we used exact value of exponential term will get exact answer).

One of the two small circular coils, (none of them having any self - inductance) is suspended with a V-shaped copper wire, with plane horizontal. Force is proportional to $\mathrm{d}^{-2}$

questions.q: A charge $Q$ is uniformly distributed over the surface of non conducting disc of radius $R$. The disc rotates about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre with an angular velocity $\omega$. As a result of this rotation a magnetic field of induction $B$ is obtained at the centre of the disc. If we keep both the amount of charge placed on the disc and its angular velocity to be constant and vary the radius of the disc then the variation of the magnetic induction at the centre of the disc will be represented by the figure
questions.solution: Consider ring like element of disc of radius $r$ and thickness $\mathrm{dr}$. If $\sigma$ is charge per unit area, then charge on the element $d q=\sigma(2 \pi r d r)$ current ' $i$ ' associated with rotating charge $\mathrm{dq}$ is $\mathrm{i}=\frac{(\mathrm{dq}) \mathrm{w}}{2 \pi}=\sigma \mathrm{wrdr}$ Magnetic field $\mathrm{dB}$ at center due to element $\mathrm{dB}=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{2 \mathrm{r}}=\frac{\mu_0 \sigma \omega \mathrm{dr}}{2} \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_{\text{net }}=\int \mathrm{dB}=\frac{\mu_0 \sigma \omega}{2} \int_0^{\mathrm{R}} \mathrm{dr}=\frac{\mu_0 \sigma \omega \mathrm{R}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{B}_{\text{net }}=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{Q} \omega}{2 \pi \mathrm{R}} \quad\left[\because \mathrm{Q}=\sigma \pi \mathrm{R}^2\right] \end{aligned}$ So if $Q and w$ are unchanged then $\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{net}} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}$ Hence variation of $B_{\text{net }}$ with $R$ should be a rectangular hyperbola as represented in (A).

Using formula $B=\frac{\mu_0^{\text{II }}}{2\left(R^2+X^2\right)^{3 / 2}}$, we get

54=$\frac{\mu_0 i(3)^2}{2\left[(3)^2+(4)^2\right]^{3 / 2}}$At the centre of the coil, $X=0$ and $B=\frac{\mu_0 i}{2(3)}$
Using equation (i)

B=$\frac{54 \times 5^3}{(3)^2 \times 3} \Rightarrow$B=250 \mu $\mathrm{T} \text{. }$
